translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 110

sentences.zh: 【晉紀三十二】 著雍閹茂，一年。

translations.literal: Jin Annals 32 — Wuyin, one year.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Annals, Part 32 — the wuyin cycle year, one year.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝乙隆安二年（

translations.literal: The second year of Long'an of Emperor An Yi (
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Long'an under Emperor An Yi (

sentences.zh: 戊戌，公元三九八年）

translations.literal: wuxu, corresponding to the year 398 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year wuxu, equivalent to 398 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，燕范陽王德自鄴帥戶四萬南徙滑台。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Murong De, Prince of Fanyang of Yan, led forty thousand households south from Ye to relocate at Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, in the first month, Murong De, Prince of Fanyang of Yan, led forty thousand households out of Ye and moved south to Huatai.

sentences.zh: 魏衛王儀入鄴，收其倉庫。

translations.literal: Murong Yi, Prince of Wei, entered Ye and seized its storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yi, the Wei prince serving under the Northern Wei, entered Ye and took possession of its granaries.

sentences.zh: 追德至河，弗及。

translations.literal: They pursued De to the river but did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: They chased Murong De as far as the river but failed to catch him.

sentences.zh: 趙王麟上尊號於德，德用兄垂故事，稱燕王，改永康三年為元年，以統府行帝制，置百官。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao, Murong Lin, offered Murong De an honorific title; De followed the precedent of his elder brother Chui, styled himself King of Yan, changed the third year of Yongkang to Year One, administered through his commandery headquarters as though wielding imperial authority, and installed the full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin, Prince of Zhao, urged Murong De to accept a supreme title. De followed the precedent set by his brother Murong Chui, took the title King of Yan, renamed the third year of Yongkang as his first year, governed from his headquarters as if holding the throne, and appointed officials throughout the administration.

sentences.zh: 以趙王麟為司空、領尚書令，慕容法為中軍將軍，慕輿拔為尚書左僕射，丁通為右僕射。

translations.literal: He appointed Murong Lin, Prince of Zhao, as Minister of Works and concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing; Murong Fa as General of the Central Army; Muyu Ba as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; and Ding Tong as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He made Murong Lin, Prince of Zhao, Minister of Works and Superintendent of the Masters of Writing; Murong Fa, General of the Central Army; Muyu Ba, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; and Ding Tong, Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 麟復謀反，德殺之。

translations.literal: Lin rebelled again; De executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin plotted rebellion once more, De put him to death.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏王珪自中山南巡至高邑，得王永之子憲，喜曰：「王景略之孫也。」

translations.literal: On gengzi day, the King of Wei, Tuoba Gui, toured south from Zhongshan to Gaoyi, captured Wang Yong's son Xian, and said with delight, "He is the grandson of Wang Meng."
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, Tuoba Gui, King of Wei, marched south from Zhongshan as far as Gaoyi, where he took Wang Yong's son Xian prisoner. Delighted, he said, "This is the grandson of Wang Meng."

sentences.zh: 以為本州中正，領選曹事，兼掌門下。

translations.literal: He appointed him Director of Selection for the native province, put him in charge of the Bureau of Selection, and gave him concurrent authority over the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xian Director of Selection for his home province, placed him in charge of the Bureau of Selection, and gave him concurrent duties in the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 至鄴，置行台，以龍驤將軍日南公和跋為尚書，與左丞賈彝帥吏兵五千人鎮鄴。

translations.literal: When he reached Ye, he established a mobile headquarters, appointed He Ba, Duke of Rinan and General of the Dragon Cavalry, as Master of Writing, and together with the Left Assistant Minister Jia Yi led five thousand clerks and troops to garrison Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye he set up a mobile headquarters, named He Ba, Duke of Rinan and a dragon-cavalry general, Master of Writing, and sent him with the Left Assistant Minister Jia Yi and five thousand officials and soldiers to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 珪自鄴還中山，將北歸，發卒萬人治直道，自望都鑿恆嶺至代五百餘里。

translations.literal: Gui returned from Ye to Zhongshan and, about to go north, mobilized ten thousand laborers to build a straight road, cutting through the Heng Mountains from Wangdu to Dai for more than five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Gui went back from Ye to Zhongshan and, preparing to return north, drafted ten thousand men to cut a straight road through the Heng range from Wangdu to Dai — more than five hundred li in all.

sentences.zh: 珪恐已既去，山東有變，復置行台於中山，命衛王儀鎮之；

translations.literal: Gui feared that after he had left, the lands east of the mountains might rise in revolt, so he again established a mobile headquarters at Zhongshan and ordered Murong Yi, Prince of Wei, to garrison it;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing trouble in the eastern provinces once he had gone, Gui re-established a mobile headquarters at Zhongshan and left Murong Yi, Prince of Wei, to hold it;

sentences.zh: 以撫軍大將軍略陽公遵為尚書左僕射，鎮勃海之合口。

translations.literal: he appointed Zun, Duke of Lueyang and General Who Pacifies the Army, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, to garrison Hekou in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: he named Zun, Duke of Lueyang and a pacifying-army general, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and stationed him at Hekou in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 右將軍尹國督租於冀州，聞珪將北還，謀襲信都；

translations.literal: The Right General Yin Guo, who was supervising tax collection in Jizhou, heard that Gui was about to return north and plotted to seize Xindu;
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guo, the Right General, was supervising tax collection in Jizhou. Learning that Gui was heading north, he plotted to seize Xindu;

sentences.zh: 安南將軍長孫嵩執國，斬之。

translations.literal: the General Who Pacifies the South, Changsun Song, seized Guo and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: but Changsun Song, the Pacifying-the-South General, arrested him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 燕啟倫還至龍城，言中山已陷；

translations.literal: Murong Qilun returned to Longcheng and reported that Zhongshan had fallen;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Qilun returned to Longcheng with word that Zhongshan had fallen;

sentences.zh: 燕主寶命罷兵。

translations.literal: the Yan ruler Murong Bao ordered the armies disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: and the Yan ruler Murong Bao ordered the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 遼西王農言於寶曰：「今遷都尚新，未可南征，宜因成師襲庫莫奚，取其牛馬以充軍資，更審虛實，俟明年而議之。」

translations.literal: Murong Nong, Prince of Liaoxi, said to Bao, "The capital has only just been moved and is not yet settled; a southern campaign is inadvisable. We should take advantage of our assembled army to strike the Kumo Xi, seize their cattle and horses to replenish our supplies, reassess the situation, and defer further plans until next year."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong, Prince of Liaoxi, told Bao, "We have only just moved the capital and cannot yet march south. Better to use the army we already have to strike the Kumo Xi, take their herds to fill our stores, and wait until next year, when we know the true situation, before deciding again."

sentences.zh: 寶從之。

translations.literal: Bao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao agreed.

sentences.zh: 己未，北行。

translations.literal: On jiwei day they marched north.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day the court moved north.

sentences.zh: 庚申，渡澆洛水。

translations.literal: On gengshen day they crossed the Qiaoluo River.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day they crossed the Qiaoluo River.

sentences.zh: 會南燕王德遣侍郎李延詣寶，言：「涉珪西上，中國空虛。」

translations.literal: Just then Murong De, King of Southern Yan, sent the Attendant Gentleman Li Yan to Bao, saying, "Tuoba Gui has gone west; the central provinces lie empty."
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Murong De of Southern Yan sent the Attendant Gentleman Li Yan to Bao with the message, "Tuoba Gui has marched west, and the heartland lies undefended."

sentences.zh: 延追寶及之，寶大喜，即日引還。

translations.literal: Yan overtook Bao and delivered the message; Bao was greatly pleased and turned back the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Yan caught up with Bao and delivered the news. Overjoyed, Bao turned the army around that very day.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，魏王珪發中山，徙山東六州吏民雜夷十餘萬口以實代。

translations.literal: On xinyou day the King of Wei, Tuoba Gui, departed Zhongshan and relocated more than a hundred thousand households of officials, commoners, and various foreign peoples from the six eastern provinces to populate Dai.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day Tuoba Gui left Zhongshan and moved more than a hundred thousand officials, commoners, and mixed populations from the six eastern provinces north to settle Dai.

sentences.zh: 博陵、勃海、章武群盜並起，略陽公遵等討平之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose together in Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu; Zun, Duke of Lueyang, and others suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit bands erupted across Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu; Zun, Duke of Lueyang, and others put them down.

sentences.zh: 廣川太守賀賴盧，性豪健，恥居冀州刺史王輔之下，襲輔，殺之，驅勒守兵，掠陽平、頓丘諸郡，南渡河，奔南燕。

translations.literal: He Lailu, Administrator of Guangchuan, was bold and fierce by nature and ashamed to serve under Wang Fu, Inspector of Jizhou; he attacked Fu, killed him, drove the garrison troops, raided the commanderies of Yangping and Dunqiu, crossed the river south, and fled to Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He Lailu, the Guangchuan administrator, was proud and combative and resented serving under Wang Fu, the Jizhou inspector. He ambushed Fu, killed him, pressed the local garrisons into his service, plundered Yangping and Dunqiu, crossed the Yellow River southward, and fled to Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 南燕王德以賴盧為并州刺史，封廣寧王。

translations.literal: Murong De, King of Southern Yan, appointed Lailu Inspector of Bingzhou and enfeoffed him as Prince of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De made Lailu inspector of Bingzhou and enfeoffed him as Prince of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸遣乞伏益州攻涼支陽、鸇武、允吾三城，克之，虜萬餘人而去。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, King of Western Qin, sent Qifu Yizhou to attack the three cities of Zhiyang, Guanwu, and Yunwu in Liang; he captured them, took more than ten thousand captives, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui of Western Qin sent Qifu Yizhou against the Liang cities of Zhiyang, Guanwu, and Yunwu. Yizhou took all three, carried off more than ten thousand people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶還龍城宮，詔諸軍就頓，不聽罷散，文武將士皆以家屬隨駕。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Murong Bao returned to the palace at Longcheng, ordered all armies to assemble at their encampments, forbade disbandment, and required civil and military officers and soldiers to bring their families with the imperial train.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao returned to the Longcheng palace, ordered every army to concentrate at its camp, forbade anyone to disband, and required officials and soldiers alike to march with their families in tow.

sentences.zh: 遼西王農、長樂王盛切諫，以為：「兵疲力弱，魏新得志，未可與敵，宜且養兵觀釁。」

translations.literal: Murong Nong, Prince of Liaoxi, and Murong Sheng, Prince of Changle, remonstrated urgently, saying, "The troops are exhausted and weak; Wei has just tasted victory and cannot yet be confronted. We should rest the army and watch for an opening."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong of Liaoxi and Murong Sheng of Changle pleaded urgently against the move: "Our soldiers are spent, and Wei is riding a fresh triumph — we cannot fight them yet. Hold the army in reserve and watch for a chance."

sentences.zh: 寶將從之，撫軍將軍慕輿騰曰：「百姓可與樂成，難與圖始。

translations.literal: Bao was about to agree when the General Who Pacifies the Army, Muyu Teng, said, "The people can share in the completion of a task but are hard to enlist at its beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was on the verge of agreeing when Muyu Teng, the Pacifying-the-Army General, said, "The people are glad to enjoy success but reluctant to embark on a hard beginning.

sentences.zh: 今師眾已集，宜獨決聖心，乘機進取，不宜廣采異同以沮大計。」

translations.literal: The army is already assembled; Your Majesty should decide alone in your sacred mind, seize the moment to advance, and not gather many dissenting views to thwart the great plan."
translations.idiomatic: The host is already gathered. Your Majesty should decide alone, strike while the moment favors us, and not let a chorus of second thoughts wreck the grand design."

sentences.zh: 寶乃曰：「吾計決矣，敢諫者斬！」

translations.literal: Bao then said, "My mind is made up; whoever dares remonstrate shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao declared, "My decision stands. Anyone who dares object will be executed!"

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，寶出就頓，留盛統後事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yihai day, Bao went out to the encampment and left Sheng in charge of affairs behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yihai day, Bao left for the camp and left Sheng to manage affairs at home.

sentences.zh: 己卯，燕軍發龍城，慕輿騰為前軍，司空農為中軍，寶為後軍，相去各一頓，連營百里。

translations.literal: On jimao day the Yan army set out from Longcheng: Muyu Teng led the vanguard, the Minister of Works Nong the center, and Bao the rear; each section was one day's march apart, and the encampments stretched for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day the Yan army marched out of Longcheng with Muyu Teng in the van, Murong Nong the Minister of Works in the center, and Bao in the rear. Each wing was a full day's march from the next, and the camps ran in an unbroken line for a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 壬午，寶至乙連，長上段速骨、宋赤眉等因眾心之憚征役，遂作亂。

translations.literal: On renwu day Bao reached Yilian; Duan Subone, Song Chimei, and other senior officers, exploiting the troops' dread of the campaign, rose in mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Bao reached Yilian. Duan Subone, Song Chimei, and other senior officers, playing on the army's fear of forced service, mutinied.

sentences.zh: 速骨等皆高陽王隆舊隊，共逼立隆子高陽王崇為主，殺樂浪威王宙、中牟熙公段誼及宗室諸王。

translations.literal: Subone and the others had all belonged to the old command of Murong Long, Prince of Gaoyang; together they forced Murong Chong, Prince of Gaoyang and Long's son, to be their leader, and killed Murong Zhou, Prince of Lelang; Duan Yi, Duke of Zhongmou; and various princes of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Subone's men had served under Murong Long, Prince of Gaoyang. They forced Long's son Murong Chong, also Prince of Gaoyang, onto the throne and murdered Murong Zhou, Prince of Lelang; Duan Yi, Duke of Zhongmou; and a number of royal princes.

sentences.zh: 河間王熙素與崇善，崇擁佑之，故獨得免。

translations.literal: Murong Xi, Prince of Hejian, had always been on good terms with Chong; Chong shielded him, and he alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xi of Hejian had long been close to Chong, who protected him, and he alone escaped death.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶將十餘騎奔司空農營，農將出迎，左右抱其腰，止之，曰：「宜小清澄，不可便出。」

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Murong Bao fled with a dozen horsemen to Minister of Works Nong's camp. Nong was about to go out to receive him when his attendants seized him around the waist and stopped him, saying, "The situation must first be clarified a little; you must not go out at once."
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled with a dozen riders to Nong's camp. Nong was about to ride out to meet him when his attendants seized him around the waist and said, "Wait until the situation is clearer — you must not go out yet."

sentences.zh: 農引刀將斫之，遂出見寶，又馳信追慕輿騰。

translations.literal: Nong drew his sword as if to strike them, then went out to see Bao and also sent a fast messenger to summon Muyu Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Nong half drew his sword as if to cut them down, then went out to Bao and sent a courier racing after Muyu Teng.

sentences.zh: 癸未，寶、農引兵還趣大營，討速骨等。

translations.literal: On guimao day Bao and Nong led troops back toward the main camp to attack Subone and the others.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Bao and Nong turned back toward the main camp to suppress Subone and his rebels.

sentences.zh: 農營兵亦厭征役，皆棄仗走，騰營亦潰。

translations.literal: The soldiers in Nong's camp also loathed the campaign and all threw down their weapons and fled; Teng's camp collapsed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Nong's troops, no less sick of the campaign, threw down their arms and ran; Teng's camp broke apart too.

sentences.zh: 寶、農奔還龍城。

translations.literal: Bao and Nong fled back to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and Nong fled back to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 長樂王盛聞亂，引兵出迎，寶、農僅而得免。

translations.literal: Murong Sheng, Prince of Changle, heard of the turmoil, led troops out to meet them, and Bao and Nong barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Sheng of Changle, hearing of the revolt, marched out to meet them, and only then did Bao and Nong escape with their lives.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子忌王、殷之逼，以譙王尚之及弟休之有才略，引為腹心。

translations.literal: Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, resented the pressure from the Wang and Yin clans; because Sima Shangzhi, Prince of Qiao, and his younger brother Xiuzhi were talented and resourceful, he drew them in as trusted confidants.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, chafed at the pressure from the Wang and Yin families. He took Sima Shangzhi of Qiao and his brother Xiuzhi — both capable men — into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 尚之說道子曰：「今方鎮強盛，宰相權輕，宜密樹腹心於外以自籓衛。」

translations.literal: Shangzhi said to Daozi, "Regional commanderies are strong today while the chief minister's authority is light; you should secretly plant trusted men in the provinces to serve as your own protective screen."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi told Daozi, "The regional commanders are strong and the chief minister's hand is weak. Plant loyal men in the provinces as a private guard around you."

sentences.zh: 道子從之，以甚司馬王愉為江州刺史，都督江州及豫州之四郡軍事，用為形援，日夜與尚之謀議，以伺四方之隙。

translations.literal: Daozi followed this advice, appointed Wang Yu, Sima of Kuaiji, Inspector of Jiangzhou with command over Jiangzhou and the military affairs of four commanderies in Yuzhou, used him as a visible support, and day and night plotted with Shangzhi to watch for openings throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi agreed. He made Wang Yu, the Kuaiji marshal, inspector of Jiangzhou with authority over Jiangzhou and four Yuzhou commanderies, posted him as open support, and spent day and night with Shangzhi plotting how to exploit any crack in the empire.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪如繁畤宮，給新徙民田及牛。

translations.literal: The King of Wei, Tuoba Gui, went to the Fanchi Palace and granted fields and oxen to the newly relocated population.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui went to the Fanchi Palace and allotted fields and oxen to the newly resettled families.

sentences.zh: 珪畋於白登山，見熊將數子，謂冠軍將軍於栗磾曰：「卿名勇健，能搏此乎？」

translations.literal: While hunting on Mount Bai, Gui saw a bear with several cubs and said to Yu Liudi, General Who Conquers the Enemy, "Your name speaks of courage and strength — can you wrestle this beast?"
translations.idiomatic: Hunting on Mount Bai, Gui saw a bear with her cubs and asked Yu Liudi, the conquering-champion general, "Your name means courage — can you wrestle that animal?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「獸賤人貴，若搏而不勝，豈不虛斃一壯士乎！」

translations.literal: He replied, "Beasts are base and men are noble; if I wrestle and fail, would I not have wasted a brave warrior for nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Beasts are low and men are high. If I fought and lost, would I not have thrown away a good soldier for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 乃驅致珪前，盡射而獲之。

translations.literal: He then drove the animals before Gui and shot them all down.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he drove the bears before the emperor and shot them all dead.

sentences.zh: 珪顧謝之。

translations.literal: Gui turned and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui thanked him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 秀容川酋長爾朱羽健從珪攻晉陽、中山有功，拜散騎常侍，環其所居，割地三百里以封之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Yuqian, chieftain of Xiurongchuan, had followed Gui in the attacks on Jinyang and Zhongshan with merit; he was appointed Palace Attendant, and the lands around his dwelling were ringed off — three hundred li were cut out to enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Yuqian, a Xiurongchuan chieftain, had served well in the campaigns against Jinyang and Zhongshan. Gui made him a palace attendant, drew a circle around his territory, and carved out three hundred li as his fief.

sentences.zh: 柔然數侵魏邊，尚書中兵郎李先請擊之。

translations.literal: The Rouran repeatedly raided Wei's borders; Li Xian, a secretary in the Central Army section of the Masters of Writing, requested an attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran kept raiding the frontier. Li Xian of the Masters of Writing's central-army section urged a punitive strike.

sentences.zh: 珪從之，大破柔然而還。

translations.literal: Gui agreed, inflicted a great defeat on the Rouran, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed, routed the Rouran decisively, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 楊軌以其司馬郭緯為西平相，帥上騎二萬北赴郭□。

translations.literal: Yang Gui appointed his Chief Clerk Guo Wei Administrator of Xiping, led twenty thousand cavalry and infantry north to reinforce Guo Nen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui named his chief clerk Guo Wei administrator of Xiping and led twenty thousand horse and foot north to join Guo Nen.

sentences.zh: 禿髮鳥孤遣其弟車騎將軍辱檀帥騎一萬助軌。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu sent his younger brother Tufa Rutan, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, with ten thousand horsemen to assist Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu sent his brother Tufa Rutan, the chariots-and-cavalry general, with ten thousand riders to help Yang Gui.

sentences.zh: 軌至姑臧，營於城北。

translations.literal: Gui reached Guzang and encamped north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui reached Guzang and pitched camp north of the walls.

sentences.zh: 燕尚書頓丘王蘭汗陰與段速骨等通謀，引兵營東城之東。

translations.literal: Murong Lanhan, Prince of Dunqiu and Master of Writing of Yan, secretly conspired with Duan Subone and others, led troops, and encamped east of the eastern wall of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lanhan of Dunqiu, a Yan Master of Writing, plotted secretly with Duan Subone and camped his force east of the eastern city wall.

sentences.zh: 城中留守兵少，長樂王盛徙內近城之民，得丁夫萬餘，乘城以御之。

translations.literal: Few troops remained to guard the city; Murong Sheng, Prince of Changle, moved the people living near the inner walls and mustered more than ten thousand able-bodied men to man the ramparts in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison inside was thin. Murong Sheng of Changle moved the population near the inner walls into service and raised more than ten thousand men to hold the battlements.

sentences.zh: 速骨等同謀才百餘人，餘皆為所驅脅，莫有鬥志。

translations.literal: Only a little more than a hundred men were Subone's fellow conspirators; the rest had all been coerced and had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a hundred men were Subone's true conspirators; the rest had been dragooned and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲午，速骨等將攻城，遼西桓烈王農恐不能守，且為蘭汗所誘，夜，潛出赴之，冀以自全。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiawu day, Subone and the others were about to assault the city; Murong Nong, Prince of Liaoxi and titled Huanlie, feared he could not hold out and, having also been enticed by Lanhan, slipped out by night to join them, hoping to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu day, Subone prepared to storm the city. Murong Nong of Liaoxi, styled Huanlie, feared the walls would not hold and, seduced by Lanhan, slipped out by night to join the rebels in hope of saving himself.

sentences.zh: 明旦，速骨等攻城，城上拒戰甚力，速骨之眾死者以百數。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Subone and the others attacked; the defenders on the walls resisted fiercely, and Subone's men died by the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Subone attacked. The defenders fought back hard, and his men fell by the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 速骨乃將農循城，農素有忠節威名，城中之眾恃以為強，忽見在城下，無不驚愕喪氣，遂皆逃潰。

translations.literal: Subone then led Nong around the wall; Nong had long enjoyed a reputation for loyalty and integrity, and the people in the city had relied on that strength — when they suddenly saw him below the wall, none failed to be stunned and lose heart, and all fled in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Subone then paraded Nong along the wall. Nong's name for loyalty had been the city's strength; when the defenders saw him below the ramparts, their spirit broke and they scattered.

sentences.zh: 速骨入城，縱兵殺掠，死者狼籍。

translations.literal: Subone entered the city and let his troops slaughter and plunder; the dead lay strewn everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Subone entered the city and let his soldiers kill and loot until the streets were heaped with corpses.

sentences.zh: 寶、盛與慕輿騰、餘崇、張真、李旱、趙恩等輕騎南走。

translations.literal: Bao, Sheng, Muyu Teng, Yu Chong, Zhang Zhen, Li Han, Zhao En, and others fled south with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, Sheng, Muyu Teng, Yu Chong, Zhang Zhen, Li Han, Zhao En, and others fled south with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 速骨幽農於殿內。

translations.literal: Subone imprisoned Nong inside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Subone shut Nong up inside the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 長上阿交羅，速骨之謀主也，以高陽王崇幼弱，更欲立農。

translations.literal: The senior officer Ajiaoluo, Subone's chief plotter, considered Murong Chong, Prince of Gaoyang, too young and weak and wished instead to set up Nong.
translations.idiomatic: Ajiaoluo, a senior officer and Subone's chief strategist, thought Murong Chong of Gaoyang too young and wanted Nong on the throne instead.

sentences.zh: 崇親信鬷讓、出力犍等聞之，丁酉，殺羅及農。

translations.literal: Chong's trusted followers Zong Rang, Chuli Jian, and others heard of this; on dingyou day they killed Ajiaoluo and Nong.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's confidants Zong Rang and Chuli Jian learned of the plot. On dingyou day they killed Ajiaoluo and Nong.

sentences.zh: 速骨即為之誅讓等。

translations.literal: Subone immediately executed Rang and the others on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Subone immediately executed Rang and his fellows in reprisal.

sentences.zh: 農故吏左衛將軍宇文拔亡奔遼西。

translations.literal: Yuwen Ba, a former subordinate of Nong and General of the Left Guard, fled to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ba, once Nong's officer and now a left-guard general, escaped to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 庚子，蘭汗襲擊速骨，並其黨盡殺之。

translations.literal: On gengzi day Lanhan launched a surprise attack on Subone and killed him and all his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Lanhan struck Subone by surprise and killed him and every one of his followers.

sentences.zh: 廢崇，奉太子策，承製大赦，遣使迎寶，及於薊城。

translations.literal: He deposed Chong, enthroned the Crown Prince Ce in his place, issued a general amnesty by imperial order, and sent envoys to welcome Bao, meeting him at Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He deposed Chong, set Crown Prince Ce on the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty in the emperor's name, and sent envoys to meet Bao at Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 寶欲全還，長樂王盛等皆曰：「汗之忠詐未可知，今單騎赴之，萬一汗有異志，悔之無及。

translations.literal: Bao wished to return in full; Murong Sheng, Prince of Changle, and others all said, "Lanhan's loyalty or treachery cannot yet be known; if you now go alone to him and he should harbor other designs, it will be too late for regret.
translations.idiomatic: Bao wanted to go straight home. Murong Sheng of Changle and the others warned, "We cannot yet tell whether Lanhan is loyal or false. Ride in alone and, if he turns on you, there will be no undoing it.

sentences.zh: 不如南就范陽王，合眾以取冀州；

translations.literal: Better to go south to Murong De, Prince of Fanyang, gather forces, and seize Jizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Better to join Murong De in the south, rally an army, and try for Jizhou;

sentences.zh: 若其不捷，收南方之眾，徐歸龍都，亦未晚也。」

translations.literal: if that fails, gather the southern hosts and slowly return to Longdu — that would not yet be too late."
translations.idiomatic: and if that fails, gather the southern armies and only then return to Longdu at leisure."

sentences.zh: 寶從之。

translations.literal: Bao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao took their advice.

sentences.zh: 離石胡帥呼延鐵、西河胡帥張崇等不樂徙代，聚眾叛魏，魏安遠將軍庾岳討平之。

translations.literal: Huyan Tie, chieftain of the Hu of Lishi, Zhang Chong, chieftain of the Hu of Xihe, and others, unwilling to be relocated to Dai, gathered followers and rebelled against Wei; Yu Yue, General Who Pacifies the Distance, suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan Tie of Lishi and Zhang Chong of Xihe, chieftains of the Hu peoples, refused relocation to Dai, rose in revolt, and were crushed by Yu Yue, the Pacifying-the-Distance General.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪召見王儀入輔，以略陽公遵代鎮中山。

translations.literal: The King of Wei, Tuoba Gui, summoned Murong Yi to court to assist him and replaced him at Zhongshan with Zun, Duke of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui recalled Murong Yi to court as an adviser and left Zun, Duke of Lueyang, to hold Zhongshan in his place.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬戌，以征虜將軍穆崇為太尉，安南將軍長孫嵩為司徒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renxu day, Mu Chong, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was appointed Grand Commandant, and Changsun Song, General Who Pacifies the South, was appointed Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renxu day, Mu Chong, the barbarian-conquering general, became Grand Commandant and Changsun Song, the Pacifying-the-South General, became Grand Minister.

sentences.zh: 燕主寶從間道過鄴，鄴人請留，寶不許。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Murong Bao passed Ye by a hidden route; the people of Ye asked him to stay, but Bao refused.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao slipped past Ye by a back road. The townspeople begged him to remain, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 南至黎陽，伏於河西，遣中黃門令趙思告北地王鐘曰：「上以二月得丞相表，即時南征，至乙連，會長上作亂，失據來此。

translations.literal: Going south to Liyang, he lay concealed west of the river and sent the Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhao Si to tell Murong Zhong, Prince of Beidi, "The Emperor received the Chancellor's memorial in the second month and at once marched south; at Yilian the senior officers mutinied, and having lost our footing we have come here.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south at Liyang he hid west of the river and sent the palace attendant Zhao Si to Murong Zhong of Beidi with the message, "The Emperor received the Chancellor's report in the second month and marched south at once. At Yilian the senior officers mutinied, and we have come here stripped of our base.

sentences.zh: 王亟白丞相奉迎！」

translations.literal: Prince, report this at once to the Chancellor and ask him to come welcome the Emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Tell the Chancellor immediately to come and welcome the throne!"

sentences.zh: 鐘，德之從弟也，首勸德稱尊號，聞而惡之，執思付獄，以狀白南燕王德。

translations.literal: Zhong was De's younger cousin and had been the first to urge De to assume an imperial title; hearing this, he was disgusted, seized Si and put him in prison, and reported the matter to Murong De, King of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was De's cousin and had been first to urge De to take the throne. Disgusted, he arrested Si, threw him in prison, and reported everything to Murong De.

sentences.zh: 德謂群下曰：「卿等以社稷大計，勸吾攝政；

translations.literal: De said to his assembled ministers, "You urged me to assume regency for the sake of the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: De told his ministers, "You pressed me to govern for the sake of the realm;

sentences.zh: 吾亦以嗣帝播越，民神乏主，故權順群議以系眾心。

translations.literal: I too saw the heir emperor cast into exile and the people and spirits left without a lord, so I provisionally followed your counsel to steady the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I too saw the heir driven into exile with no ruler for the people or the spirits, and I bowed to your counsel for the moment to steady their hearts.

sentences.zh: 今天方悔禍，嗣帝得還，吾將具法駕奉迎，謝罪行闕，何如？」

translations.literal: Now Heaven has turned from its calamity and the heir emperor can return; I shall prepare the full imperial equipage to welcome him and go to the palace gates to confess my fault — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has turned from disaster and the heir can return. I will go out with the full imperial escort to welcome him and kneel at the palace gate to confess my fault. What say you?"

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎張華曰：「今天下大亂，非雄才無以寧濟群生。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua, Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate, said, "The realm is in great disorder today; without a heroic talent the people cannot be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua of the Yellow Gate said, "The empire is in chaos. Only a heroic ruler can save the people.

sentences.zh: 嗣帝暗懦，不能紹隆先統。

translations.literal: The heir emperor is dim and weak and cannot continue and exalt the former imperial line.
translations.idiomatic: The heir is dull and timid and cannot carry on the ancestral mandate.

sentences.zh: 陛下若蹈匹夫之節，捨天授之業，威權一去，身首不保，況社稷其得血食乎！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows the scruples of a common man and abandons the enterprise Heaven has conferred, once authority departs you will not keep body or head — how much less will the altars of state continue to receive blood sacrifice!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty clings to private scruple and casts away Heaven's mandate, your power will vanish, your life will not be safe, and the imperial altars will cease to receive sacrifice!"

sentences.zh: 慕輿護曰：「嗣帝不達時宜，委棄國都，自取敗亡，不堪多難，亦已明矣。

translations.literal: Muyu Hu said, "The heir emperor does not grasp the needs of the age; he abandoned the capital and brought defeat on himself — it is already clear that he cannot bear many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Muyu Hu said, "The heir misread the times, abandoned the capital, and courted ruin. It is plain he cannot weather further disaster.

sentences.zh: 昔蒯聵出奔，衛輒不納，《春秋》是之。

translations.literal: In former times Kuai Kui went into exile and Wei Zhe would not receive him — the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 approved this.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuai Kui fled, Wei Zhe refused him entry, and the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 approved.

sentences.zh: 以子拒父猶可，況以父拒子乎！

translations.literal: If a son may reject his father, how much more may a father reject his son!
translations.idiomatic: If a son may turn away his father, how much more may a father turn away his son!

sentences.zh: 今趙思之言，未明虛實，臣請為陛下馳往詗之。」

translations.literal: Zhao Si's words today have not yet clarified truth from falsehood; I ask to ride swiftly on Your Majesty's behalf to investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Si's tale may be true or false. Let me ride north at once and learn the facts for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 德流涕遣之。

translations.literal: De wept as he sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: De wept as he sent Hu on his way.

sentences.zh: 護帥壯士數百人，隨思而北，聲言迎衛，其實圖之。

translations.literal: Hu led several hundred stalwarts north after Si, proclaiming that he was going to welcome the heir, but in truth plotting against him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu took several hundred picked men north behind Si, claiming he meant to welcome the heir but in truth plotting his destruction.

sentences.zh: 寶既遣思詣鐘，於後得樵者，言德已稱制，懼而北走。

translations.literal: After Bao had sent Si to Zhong, he afterward obtained a woodcutter who said De had already assumed imperial authority; afraid, he fled north.
translations.idiomatic: After Bao had sent Si to Zhong, he later met a woodcutter who said De had already taken the throne. Terrified, he turned north and fled.

sentences.zh: 護至，無所見，執思以還。

translations.literal: Hu arrived, found nothing, seized Si and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hu got there, found no heir to welcome, seized Zhao Si, and marched back.

sentences.zh: 德以思練習典故，欲留而用之。

translations.literal: De, because Si was versed in classical precedents, wished to keep him and employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De saw that Zhao Si knew the ritual canon well and wanted to keep him in service.

sentences.zh: 思曰：「犬馬猶知戀主，思雖刑臣，乞還就上。」

translations.literal: Si said, "Even dogs and horses know to cling to their master; though Si is a punished official, I beg to return and join my sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "Even dogs and horses know loyalty to their master. Though I am a disgraced minister, I beg leave to go back and serve my lord."

sentences.zh: 德固留之，思怒曰：「周室東遷，晉、鄭是依。

translations.literal: De forcibly detained him. Si angrily said, "When the Zhou house moved east, it relied on Jin and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: De would not let him go. Si flared in anger: "When the Zhou court moved east, it leaned on Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 殿下親則叔父，位為上公，不能帥先群後以匡帝室，而幸本根之傾，為趙王倫之事，思雖不能如申包胥之存楚，猶慕龔君賓不偷生莽世也！」

translations.literal: Your Highness is the Emperor's uncle by kin and holds the rank of Grand Duke; you cannot lead those before and those after to restore the imperial house, yet rejoice at the overturning of the root and do as Prince Lun of Zhao did! Though Si cannot be like Shen Baoxu in saving Chu, I still admire Gong Junbin for refusing to live on ignobly in Wang Mang's age!"
translations.idiomatic: You are the Emperor's uncle and a Grand Duke. You ought to lead every rank, high and low, in restoring the throne, not welcome the uprooting of the dynasty and repeat the crime of Prince Lun of Zhao! I may never equal Shen Baoxu saving Chu, but I can still take Gong Junbin as my model — he would not steal life under Wang Mang!"

sentences.zh: 德斬之。

translations.literal: De executed him.
translations.idiomatic: De had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 寶遣扶風忠公慕輿騰與長樂王盛收兵冀州，盛以騰素暴橫，為民所怨，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Bao sent Muyu Teng, Duke of Zhong of Fufeng, and Murong Sheng, Prince of Changle, to gather troops in Jizhou; Sheng, because Teng had always been violent and overbearing and was resented by the people, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sent Muyu Teng of Fufeng and Murong Sheng of Changle to raise troops in Jizhou. Sheng killed Teng, who had long been brutal and hated by the people.

sentences.zh: 行至巨鹿、長樂，說諸豪傑，皆願起兵奉寶。

translations.literal: When they reached Julu and Changle, they persuaded the local magnates, who all wished to raise armies and support Bao.
translations.idiomatic: At Julu and Changle they rallied the local leaders, and all pledged to take up arms for Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶以蘭汗祀燕宗廟，所為似順，意欲還龍城，不肯留冀州，乃北行。

translations.literal: Bao, because Lanhan had sacrificed at the Yan ancestral temple and his conduct seemed compliant, intended to return to Longcheng; unwilling to remain in Jizhou, he traveled north.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan had sacrificed at the Yan ancestral shrines and seemed loyal, so Bao decided to go home to Longcheng rather than hold Jizhou, and marched north.

sentences.zh: 至建安，抵民張曹家。

translations.literal: Reaching Jian'an, he lodged at the house of Zhang Cao, a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: At Jian'an he took shelter with a local man named Zhang Cao.

sentences.zh: 曹素武健，請為寶合眾，盛亦勸寶宜且駐留，察汗情狀。

translations.literal: Cao was by nature martial and strong; he asked to gather followers for Bao, and Sheng also urged Bao to halt for a time and observe Han's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Cao was a tough, capable man and offered to raise troops for Bao. Sheng likewise urged Bao to pause and learn what Lanhan was really planning.

sentences.zh: 寶乃遣冗從僕射李旱先往見汗，寶留頓石城。

translations.literal: Bao thereupon sent the supernumerary attendant-master Li Han ahead to see Han, while Bao halted at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sent Li Han ahead as envoy to Lanhan and camped at Shicheng to wait.

sentences.zh: 會汗遣左將軍蘇超奉迎，陳汗忠款。

translations.literal: Just then Han sent the Left General Su Chao to welcome him courteously and set forth Han's loyal sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan sent Left General Su Chao to welcome him and swear his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 寶以汗燕王垂之舅，盛之妃父也，謂必無它，不待旱返，遂行。

translations.literal: Bao, because Han was the maternal uncle of King Murong Chui of Yan and the father of Sheng's consort, believed there could be no other designs; without waiting for Han to return, he set out.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan was Murong Chui's uncle and Sheng's father-in-law, so Bao assumed he meant no harm. Without waiting for Li Han's report, he set out at once.

sentences.zh: 盛流涕固諫，寶不聽，留盛在後，盛與將軍張真下道避匿。

translations.literal: Sheng wept and remonstrated firmly; Bao would not listen, left Sheng behind, and Sheng and General Zhang Zhen left the road and hid themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng wept and pleaded in vain. Bao would not listen, kept Sheng behind, and Sheng slipped off the road with General Zhang Zhen to hide.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，寶至索莫汗陘，去龍城四十里，城中皆喜。

translations.literal: On dinghai day, Bao reached Suomo Pass, forty li from Longcheng; everyone in the city rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Bao reached Suomo Pass, forty li from Longcheng, and the city erupted in joy.

sentences.zh: 汗惶怖，欲自出請罪，兄弟共諫止之。

translations.literal: Han was alarmed and afraid, and wished to go out himself to beg forgiveness; his brothers jointly remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan panicked and wanted to go out and submit. His brothers talked him out of it.

sentences.zh: 汗乃遣弟加難帥五百騎出迎，又遣兄堤閉門止仗，禁人出入。

translations.literal: Han then sent his younger brother Jianan leading five hundred horsemen out to welcome him, and also sent his elder brother Di to close the gates, halt weapons, and forbid people from entering or leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan sent his brother Jianan out with five hundred horse to welcome Bao, and ordered his brother Di to shut the gates, stand the garrison down, and seal the city.

sentences.zh: 城中皆知其將為變，而無如之何。

translations.literal: Everyone in the city knew a coup was coming, yet could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The whole city knew treachery was afoot, but no one could stop it.

sentences.zh: 加難見寶於陘北，拜謁已，從寶俱進。

translations.literal: Jianan met Bao north of the pass; after bowing in audience, he advanced together with Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Jianan met Bao north of the pass, paid his respects, and rode on with him.

sentences.zh: 穎陰烈公餘崇密言於寶曰：「觀加難形色，禍變甚逼，宜留三思，奈何徑前！」

translations.literal: Yu Chong, Duke of Lie of Yingyin, secretly said to Bao, "Judging by Jianan's appearance, calamity is very near; you should pause and think thrice — why press straight ahead!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chong of Yingyin whispered to Bao, "Look at Jianan's face — disaster is close. Stop and think before you go another step!"

sentences.zh: 寶不從。

translations.literal: Bao did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Bao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 行數里，加難先執崇，崇大呼罵曰：「汝家幸緣肺腑，蒙國寵榮，覆宗不足以報。

translations.literal: After traveling several li, Jianan first seized Chong. Chong shouted and cursed, saying, "Your house, by fortune linked in flesh and bone, received the state's favor and glory — the destruction of your whole clan would not repay it.
translations.idiomatic: A few li on, Jianan seized Chong first. Chong cried out, "Fortune tied your house to the throne by blood. The state heaped honors on you — even wiping out your clan would not repay the debt.

sentences.zh: 今乃敢謀篡逆，此天地所不容，計旦慕即屠滅，但恨我不得手膾汝曹耳！」

translations.literal: Now you dare plot usurpation — this heaven and earth will not permit; I reckon you will be slaughtered by morning or evening, and only regret that I cannot with my own hands carve you all up!"
translations.idiomatic: And now you dare treason! Heaven and earth will not abide it. You will be wiped out by morning — I only regret I will not live to carve you up myself!"

sentences.zh: 加難殺之。

translations.literal: Jianan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianan cut him down.

sentences.zh: 引寶入龍城外邸，弒之。

translations.literal: He led Bao into the outer palace outside Longcheng and assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: He led Bao into an outer manor beyond Longcheng and murdered him.

sentences.zh: 汗謚寶曰靈帝，殺獻哀太子策及王公卿士百餘人，自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、昌黎王，元元青龍。

translations.literal: Han gave Bao the posthumous title Emperor Ling, killed the Crown Prince Ce of Xian'ai and more than a hundred kings, dukes, and ministers, styled himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Changli, and changed the era name to Qinglong, first year.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan gave Bao the posthumous name Emperor Ling, killed Crown Prince Ce and more than a hundred court nobles and officials, and proclaimed himself Grand Commander, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of Changli, with a new era title Qinglong.

sentences.zh: 以堤為太尉，加難為車騎將軍，封河間王熙為遼東公，如杞、宋故事。

translations.literal: He made Di Grand Commandant and Jianan General of Chariots and Cavalry; he enfeoffed Xi, Prince of Hejian, as Duke of Liaodong, following the precedent of Qi and Song.
translations.idiomatic: He made Di Grand Commandant and Jianan General of Chariots and Cavalry, and enfeoffed Prince Xi of Hejian as Duke of Liaodong after the Qi and Song precedent.

sentences.zh: 長樂王盛聞之，馳欲赴哀；

translations.literal: Murong Sheng, Prince of Changle, on hearing this, sped away wishing to go mourn;
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Sheng heard the news, he raced off to mourn;

sentences.zh: 張真止之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhen stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhen held him back.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「我今以窮歸汗。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "I now return to Han in destitution.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "I go to Lanhan now as a fugitive.

sentences.zh: 汗性愚淺，必念婚姻，不忍殺我。

translations.literal: Han is stupid and shallow by nature; he is sure to think on our marriage ties and will not bear to kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan is a simple, shallow man. He will remember we are kin by marriage and will not kill me.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，足以展吾情志。」

translations.literal: Within a month or so there will be time enough to carry out my purpose."
translations.idiomatic: A month or two will be enough for me to act."

sentences.zh: 遂往見汗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to see Han.
translations.idiomatic: And he went to see Lanhan.

sentences.zh: 汗妻乙氏及盛妃皆泣涕請盛於汗，盛妃復頓頭於諸兄弟。

translations.literal: Han's wife Lady Yi and Sheng's consort both wept and begged Han for Sheng; Sheng's consort again kowtowed before all the brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan's wife Lady Yi and Sheng's wife both wept and pleaded for Sheng. Sheng's wife kowtowed to Lanhan's brothers as well.

sentences.zh: 汗惻然哀之，乃捨盛於宮中，以為侍中、左光祿大夫，親待如舊。

translations.literal: Han was moved with pity and compassion; he spared Sheng in the palace, made him Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Household Guard Grand Master, and treated him with old intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Lanhan spared Sheng and kept him in the palace as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Household Guard Grand Master, treating him as before.

sentences.zh: 堤、加難屢請殺盛，汗不從。

translations.literal: Di and Jianan repeatedly asked to kill Sheng; Han did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Di and Jianan begged repeatedly for Sheng's death, but Lanhan refused.

sentences.zh: 堤驕很荒淫，事汗多無禮，盛因而間之。

translations.literal: Di was arrogant, obstinate, and dissolute; in serving Han he was often without propriety, and Sheng used this to sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: Di was arrogant, cruel, and licentious, and often treated Lanhan disrespectfully. Sheng used that to drive a wedge between them.

sentences.zh: 由是汗兄弟浸相嫌忌。

translations.literal: From this Han's brothers gradually came to mutual suspicion and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lanhan and his brothers grew suspicious and resentful of one another.

sentences.zh: 涼太原公纂將兵擊楊軌，郭□救之，纂敗還。

translations.literal: Zuan, Duke of Taiyuan of Liang, led troops to attack Yang Gui; Guo Nen rescued him, and Zuan was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan of Taiyuan marched against Yang Gui. Guo Nen came to his rescue and drove Zuan back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 段業使沮渠蒙遜攻西郡，執太守呂純以歸。

translations.literal: Duan Ye sent Juqu Mengxun to attack Xijun, seized the Administrator Lü Chun, and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye sent Juqu Mengxun against Xijun, captured Administrator Lü Chun, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 純，光之弟子也。

translations.literal: Chun was a disciple-nephew of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was Lü Guang's nephew.

sentences.zh: 於是晉昌太守王德、敦煌太守趙郡孟敏皆以郡降業。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang De, Administrator of Jinchang, and Meng Min of Zhao commandery, Administrator of Dunhuang, both surrendered their commanderies to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Jinchang administrator Wang De and the Dunhuang administrator Meng Min of Zhao both surrendered their prefectures to Duan Ye.

sentences.zh: 業封蒙遜為臨池侯，以德為酒泉太守，敏為沙州刺史。

translations.literal: Ye enfeoffed Mengxun as Marquis of Linchi, made De Administrator of Jiuquan, and Min Governor of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye enfeoffed Mengxun as Marquis of Linchi, made Wang De administrator of Jiuquan, and Meng Min governor of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，魏王珪命群臣議國號。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingzi day, Tuoba Gui, King of Wei, ordered the ministers to discuss the national designation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingzi day, Tuoba Gui ordered his ministers to debate the realm's official name.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「周、秦以前，皆自諸侯升為天子，因以其國為天下號。

translations.literal: All said, "Before Zhou and Qin, all rose from feudal lords to Son of Heaven and therefore took their state as the name for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "Before Zhou and Qin, new dynasties took their old feudal name as the name of the empire.

sentences.zh: 漢氏以來，皆無尺土之資。

translations.literal: From the Han house onward, all lacked even a foot of territory as their base.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han, founders have begun without an inch of inherited land.

sentences.zh: 我國家百世相承，開基代北，遂撫有方夏，今宜以代為號。」

translations.literal: Our state has passed down a hundred generations, established its foundation north of Dai, and now pacifies the civilized heartland; today it is fitting to take Dai as the designation."
translations.idiomatic: Our house has ruled for generations, rose in the northern Dai region, and now holds sway over the heartland. The name should be Dai."

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎崔宏曰：「昔商人不常厥居，故兩稱殷、商；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Cui Hong said, "In former times the Shang people did not dwell in one fixed place, and so were called both Yin and Shang;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong of the Yellow Gate said, "The Shang moved their seat often and were known by two names, Yin and Shang;

sentences.zh: 代雖舊邦，其命惟新，登國之妝，已更曰魏。

translations.literal: Dai, though an old domain, received a mandate wholly renewed; from the founding of the Dengguo state era, it had already been changed to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Dai is an ancient homeland, but its mandate is new — since the founding of the Dengguo state era it has already been called Wei.

sentences.zh: 夫魏者，大名，神州之上國民，宜稱魏如故。」

translations.literal: Wei is a great name and the upper state's designation among the civilized lands; it is fitting to style it Wei as before."
translations.idiomatic: Wei is a great name and the proper title for a state of the central realm. Let the name remain Wei."

sentences.zh: 珪從之。

translations.literal: Gui followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui agreed.

sentences.zh: 楊軌自恃其眾，欲與涼王光決戰，郭□每以天道抑止之。

translations.literal: Yang Gui, relying on his numbers, wished to fight a decisive battle with Lü Guang, King of Liang; Guo Nen each time restrained him by appeal to Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui, confident in his numbers, wanted a pitched battle with Lü Guang. Guo Nen repeatedly held him back, citing heaven's signs.

sentences.zh: 涼常山公弘鎮張掖，段業使沮渠男成及王德攻之；

translations.literal: Lü Hong, Duke of Changshan of Liang, held Zhangye; Duan Ye sent Juqu Nancheng and Wang De to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong of Changshan held Zhangye. Duan Ye sent Juqu Nancheng and Wang De against him;

sentences.zh: 光使太原公纂將兵迎之。

translations.literal: Guang sent Zuan, Duke of Taiyuan, to lead troops to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent Lü Zuan of Taiyuan with an army to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 楊軌曰：「呂弘精兵一萬，若與光合，則姑臧益強，不可取矣。」

translations.literal: Yang Gui said, "Lü Hong has ten thousand picked troops; if he joins with Guang, then Guzang will grow stronger still and cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui said, "Lü Hong has ten thousand elite troops. If he joins Guang, Guzang will only grow stronger and we will never take it."

sentences.zh: 乃與禿髮利鹿孤共邀擊纂，纂與戰，大破之；

translations.literal: He then joined with Tufa Lilugu in intercepting and attacking Zuan; Zuan gave battle and inflicted a great defeat on them;
translations.idiomatic: He and Tufa Lilugu ambushed Zuan's column together. Zuan gave battle and routed them;

sentences.zh: 軌奔王乞基。

translations.literal: Gui fled to Wang Qiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui fled to Wang Qiji.

sentences.zh: □性褊急殘忍，不為士民所附，聞軌敗走，降西秦。

translations.literal: Nen was by nature narrow, impatient, and cruel, and was not attached to by gentry and commoners; hearing that Gui had been defeated and fled, he surrendered to Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen was violent, petty, and cruel, and the people would not follow him. When he heard Yang Gui had been routed, he surrendered to Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾歸以為建忠將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, King of Western Qin, made him General Who Establishes Loyalty and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui of Western Qin made him General Who Establishes Loyalty and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 弘引兵棄張掖東走，段業徙治張掖，將追擊弘。

translations.literal: Hong led his army, abandoning Zhangye, and fled east; Duan Ye moved his seat of government to Zhangye and was about to pursue Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hong abandoned Zhangye and fled east. Duan Ye moved his capital to Zhangye and prepared to chase him down.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜諫曰：「歸師勿遏，窮寇勿追，兵家之戒也。」

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun remonstrated, saying, "Do not intercept a force returning home; do not pursue a desperate foe — this is a maxim of military art."
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun warned, "Never block an army going home or chase a cornered enemy — that is the first rule of war."

sentences.zh: 業不從，大敗而還，賴蒙遜以免。

translations.literal: Ye did not follow the advice, was greatly defeated and returned, and only thanks to Mengxun escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye ignored him, suffered a crushing defeat, and only Mengxun's intervention saved him.

sentences.zh: 業城西安，以其將臧莫孩為太守。

translations.literal: Ye fortified Xi'an and made his general Zang Mohai its Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye fortified Xi'an and put his general Zang Mohai in charge as administrator.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜曰：「莫孩勇而無謀，知進不知退；

translations.literal: Mengxun said, "Mohai is brave but without stratagem — he knows advance but not retreat;
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun said, "Mohai is brave but rash. He knows how to advance, not how to retreat;

sentences.zh: 此乃為之築塚，非築城也！」

translations.literal: this is building him a tomb, not building a city!"
translations.idiomatic: You are building him a grave, not a fortress!"

sentences.zh: 業不從，莫孩尋為呂纂所破。

translations.literal: Ye did not follow the advice; before long Mohai was defeated by Lü Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye paid no heed, and Mohai was soon crushed by Lü Zuan.

sentences.zh: 燕太原王奇，楷之子，蘭汗之外孫也，汗亦不殺，以為征南將軍，得入見長樂王盛。

translations.literal: Murong Qi, Prince of Taiyuan of Yan, son of Kai, was Lanhan's maternal grandson; Han likewise did not kill him, made him General Who Punishes the South, and permitted him to enter and see Murong Sheng, Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Qi of Taiyuan, son of Murong Kai and Lanhan's grandson by a daughter, was spared as well. Lanhan made him General Who Punishes the South and allowed him to visit Murong Sheng.

sentences.zh: 盛潛使奇逃出起兵。

translations.literal: Sheng secretly sent Qi to escape and raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng secretly helped Qi slip away to raise an army.

sentences.zh: 奇起兵於建安，眾至數千，汗遣蘭堤討之。

translations.literal: Qi raised troops at Jian'an; his followers reached several thousand; Han sent Lan Di to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi mustered several thousand men at Jian'an. Lanhan sent Lan Di to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 盛謂汗曰：「善駒小兒，未能辦此，豈非有假托其名欲為內應者乎！

translations.literal: Sheng said to Han, "That boy Shanju could not accomplish this — surely someone is borrowing his name wishing to serve as an inside collaborator!
translations.idiomatic: Sheng told Lanhan, "That boy Qi is too young to pull this off. Someone must be using his name to set up an inside contact!

sentences.zh: 太尉素驕，難信，不宜委以大眾。」

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant has always been arrogant, is hard to trust, and should not be entrusted with a large force."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant is arrogant and unreliable. You should not give him a large army."

sentences.zh: 汗然之，罷堤兵，更遣撫軍將軍仇尼慕將兵討奇。

translations.literal: Han agreed, dismissed Di's troops, and instead sent the Pacifying-Army General Qiu Nimuch leading troops to suppress Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan agreed, recalled Di's troops, and sent Pacifying-Army General Qiu Nimuch against Qi instead.

sentences.zh: 於是龍城自夏不雨至於秋七月，汗日詣燕諸廟及寶神座頓首禱請，委罪於蘭加難。

translations.literal: Thereupon from summer no rain fell in Longcheng until the seventh month of autumn; Han daily visited the Yan shrines and Bao's spirit seat, prostrating himself in prayer, and laid the blame on Lan Jianan.
translations.idiomatic: Longcheng had gone without rain since summer, and by the seventh month drought still held. Lanhan went daily to the Yan shrines and Murong Bao's spirit tablet to pray, blaming Lan Jianan for the calamity.

sentences.zh: 堤及加難聞之，怒，且懼誅。

translations.literal: Di and Jianan, on hearing this, were angry and also feared execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Di and Jianan heard this, they were furious — and afraid Lanhan would have them killed.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，相與帥所部襲仇尼慕軍，敗之。

translations.literal: On yisi day, they jointly led their divisions to attack Qiu Nimuch's army and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day they jointly led their troops against Qiu Nimuch and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 汗大懼，遣太子穆將兵討之。

translations.literal: Han was greatly afraid and sent the Crown Prince Mu leading troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Lanhan sent Crown Prince Murong Mu with an army to put them down.

sentences.zh: 穆謂汗曰：「慕容盛，我之仇讎，必與奇相表裡，此乃腹心之疾，不可養也，宜先除之。」

translations.literal: Mu said to Han, "Murong Sheng is my sworn enemy; he must be acting with Qi as inner and outer collaborators — this is a disease of the heart and vitals, cannot be nourished, and he should first be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Mu told Lanhan, "Murong Sheng is my bitter enemy and must be working with Qi from inside and out. That is a sickness at the heart of the realm — deal with him first."

sentences.zh: 汗欲殺盛，先引見，察之。

translations.literal: Han wished to kill Sheng; he first summoned him for an audience to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan decided to kill Sheng but summoned him first to take his measure.

sentences.zh: 盛妃知之，密以告盛，盛稱疾不出，汗亦止不殺。

translations.literal: Sheng's consort learned of it and secretly told Sheng; Sheng claimed illness and did not go out, and Han also stopped and did not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's wife learned of the plot and warned him in secret. Sheng pleaded illness and stayed away, and Lanhan held back after all.

sentences.zh: 李旱、衛雙、劉忠、張豪、張真，皆盛素所厚也，而穆引以為腹心，旱、雙得出入至盛所，潛與盛結謀。

translations.literal: Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhong, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen were all men Sheng had long favored, yet Mu drew them in as his trusted intimates; Han and Shuang were able to enter and leave Sheng's quarters and secretly joined in plotting with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhong, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen had long been close to Sheng, yet Murong Mu made them his confidants. Han and Shuang could come and go from Sheng's quarters and secretly conspired with him.

sentences.zh: 丁未，穆擊堤、加難等，破之。

translations.literal: On dingwei day, Mu attacked Di, Jianan, and the others and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Murong Mu defeated Di, Jianan, and their allies.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，饗將士，汗、穆皆醉，盛夜如廁，因逾垣入於東宮，與旱等共殺穆。

translations.literal: On gengxu day, at a feast for officers and soldiers, Han and Mu were both drunk; Sheng at night went to the privy, then climbed over the wall and entered the Eastern Palace, and together with Han and the others killed Mu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day, at a feast for the troops, Lanhan and Mu both drank deep. That night Sheng excused himself to the privy, climbed the wall into the Eastern Palace, and with Li Han and the others killed Murong Mu.

sentences.zh: 時軍未解嚴，皆聚在穆捨，聞盛得出，呼躍爭先，攻汗，斬之。

translations.literal: At that time the army had not yet been stood down from alert; all were gathered at Mu's quarters; hearing that Sheng had gotten out, they shouted and leaped, vying to be first, attacked Han, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The army was still under arms, packed around Mu's quarters. When they heard Sheng had escaped, they roared and rushed Lanhan, cutting him down.

sentences.zh: 汗子魯公和、陳公揚分屯令支、白狼，盛遣旱、真襲誅之。

translations.literal: Han's sons the Duke of Lu, He, and the Duke of Chen, Yang, were encamped separately at Lingzhi and Bailang; Sheng sent Han and Zhen to make surprise attacks and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan's sons He, Duke of Lu, and Yang, Duke of Chen, were posted at Lingzhi and Bailang. Sheng sent Li Han and Zhang Zhen to strike and kill them.

sentences.zh: 堤、加難亡匿，捕得，斬之。

translations.literal: Di and Jianan went into hiding; captured, they were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Di and Jianan hid, were caught, and were executed.

sentences.zh: 於是內外帖然，士女相慶。

translations.literal: Thereupon inner and outer were settled; gentlemen and women congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and out the realm grew calm, and men and women rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 宇文拔帥壯士數百來赴，盛拜拔為大宗正。

translations.literal: Yuwen Ba led several hundred stalwarts to come and join; Sheng appointed Ba as Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ba arrived with several hundred warriors. Sheng made him Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，告於太廟，令曰：「賴五祖之休，文武之力，宗廟社稷幽而復顯。

translations.literal: On xinhai day, he announced at the Grand Temple, decreeing, "Relying on the blessings of the five ancestors and the strength of civil and military officers, the ancestral temple and state altars, though hidden, have again been revealed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day he announced at the Grand Temple: "By the grace of five generations of ancestors and the work of civil and military men, the throne and the altars, though eclipsed, shine again.

sentences.zh: 不獨孤以眇眇之身免不同天之責，凡在臣民皆得明目當世。」

translations.literal: Not I alone, in my slight person, escape the charge of not sharing Heaven's vengeance; all ministers and people may now hold their heads high in this age."
translations.idiomatic: Not I alone, insignificant as I am, am spared the shame of living under a different sky from my father's murderer — every subject may now face the world with clear eyes."

sentences.zh: 因大赦，改元建平。

translations.literal: He thereupon granted a grand amnesty and changed the era name to Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jianping.

sentences.zh: 盛謙不敢稱尊號，以長樂王攝行統制。

translations.literal: Sheng in humility dared not assume an honorific title and, as Prince of Changle, temporarily exercised overall rule.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng modestly refused a royal title and ruled provisionally as Prince of Changle.

sentences.zh: 諸王皆降稱公，以東陽公根為尚書左僕射，衛倫、陽璆、魯恭、王騰為尚書，悅真為侍中，，陽哲為中書監，張通為中領軍，自餘文武各復舊位。

translations.literal: All princes were demoted to the title of duke; Dongyang Duke Gen was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Wei Lun, Yang Qiu, Lu Gong, and Wang Teng were made Masters of Writing; Yue Zhen was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Yang Zhe was made Director of the Palace Secretariat, Zhang Tong was made Central Army Commander; the rest of civil and military officers each resumed their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Every prince was reduced to duke. Sheng made Dongyang Duke Gen left vice director of the Masters of Writing, Wei Lun, Yang Qiu, Lu Gong, and Wang Teng masters of writing, Yue Zhen attendant-in-ordinary, and Yang Zhe director of the palace secretariat; Zhang Tong became central army commander; and the remaining officials returned to their former posts.

sentences.zh: 改謚寶曰惠閔皇帝，廟號烈宗。

translations.literal: He changed Bao's posthumous title to Emperor Huimin and his temple name to Liezong.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Bao the posthumous name Emperor Huimin and the temple name Liezong.

sentences.zh: 初，太原王奇舉兵建安，南、北之民翕然從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Murong Qi, Prince of Taiyuan, raised troops at Jian'an, the people north and south flocked to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Qi first raised his standard at Jian'an, people north and south rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗遣其兄子全討奇，奇擊滅之，匹馬不返，進屯乙連。

translations.literal: Lanhan sent his elder brother's son Quan to attack Qi; Qi struck and destroyed him, not a single horse returning; he advanced and encamped at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhan sent his nephew Quan against Qi. Qi wiped him out to the last horse and advanced to camp at Yilian.

sentences.zh: 盛既誅汗，命奇罷兵。

translations.literal: After Sheng had executed Han, he ordered Qi to disband his army.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sheng had killed Lanhan, he ordered Qi to stand his troops down.

sentences.zh: 奇用丁零嚴生、烏桓王龍之謀，遂不受命，甲寅，勒兵三萬餘人進至橫溝，去龍城十里。

translations.literal: Qi adopted the counsel of the Dingling Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan king Long; he then did not accept the order; on jiayin day he mustered more than thirty thousand men and advanced to Henggou, ten li from Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qi took the advice of the Dingling leader Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan chief Long, refused the order, and on jiayin day marched more than thirty thousand men to Henggou, ten li from Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 盛出擊，大破之，執奇而還，斬其黨百餘人，賜奇死，桓王之嗣遂絕。

translations.literal: Sheng went out to attack, inflicted a great defeat, seized Qi and returned, beheaded more than a hundred of his faction, granted Qi death by permission, and the succession of the Prince of Huan was thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng marched out, crushed him, took Qi prisoner, executed more than a hundred of his followers, granted Qi an honorable death, and with that the line of Prince Huan ended.

sentences.zh: 群臣固請上尊號，盛弗許。

translations.literal: The ministers firmly requested that he ascend to an honorific title; Sheng refused.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly pressed him to take the throne, but Sheng refused.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪遷都平城，始營宮室，建宗廟，立社稷。

translations.literal: The King of Wei, Tuoba Gui, moved the capital to Pingcheng, began constructing palaces, built ancestral temples, and established the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui, King of Wei, relocated his capital to Pingcheng, where he began building palaces, erecting ancestral temples, and founding the altars to Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 宗廟歲五祭，用分、至及臘。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple was sacrificed to five times a year, using the equinoxes and solstices and the la festival.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple received five sacrifices a year, held at the equinoxes and solstices and at the winter la festival.

sentences.zh: 桓玄求為廣州。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan requested to be assigned to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan asked to be posted to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子忌玄，不欲使居荊州，因其所欲，以玄為督交、廣二州軍事、廣州刺史；

translations.literal: Simao Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, was jealous of Xuan and did not wish him to remain in Jing Province; following what he desired, he appointed Xuan Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the two provinces of Jiao and Guang and Governor of Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Simao Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, envied Huan Xuan and did not want him to hold Jing Province. To gratify Xuan's wish, he made him Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Jiao and Guang and Governor of Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 玄受命而不行。

translations.literal: Xuan accepted the appointment but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan accepted the commission but refused to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史庾楷以道子割其四郡使王愉督之，上疏言：「江州內地，而西府北帶寇戎，不應使愉分督。」

translations.literal: Yu Kai, Inspector of Yu Province, because Daozi had carved off four of his commanderies to put Wang Yu in charge of them, submitted a memorial saying: "Jiang Province is interior territory, while the Western Headquarters on the north borders barbarian foes — Wang Yu should not be allowed supervisory authority over a portion of it."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai, Inspector of Yu, resenting Daozi's transfer of four commanderies from his jurisdiction to Wang Yu's supervision, memorialized the throne: "Jiangzhou lies in the heart of the realm, yet the western capital at Jiankang faces barbarian raiders to the north — Wang Yu ought not be given a separate command there."

sentences.zh: 朝廷不許。

translations.literal: The court did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused his request.

sentences.zh: 楷怒，遣其子鴻說王恭曰：「尚之兄弟復秉機權，過於國寶，欲假朝威削弱方鎮，懲艾前事，為禍不測。

translations.literal: Kai grew angry and sent his son Hong to persuade Wang Gong, saying: "The Shangzhi brothers have again seized the levers of power, exceeding even Wang Guobao; they wish to borrow the court's authority to weaken the regional garrisons and punish the previous affair — the resulting calamity cannot be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: In his fury Kai sent his son Hong to Wang Gong with a warning: "The Shangzhi brothers have taken power again, and they surpass even Wang Guobao in arrogance. They mean to use the court's authority to strip the provinces of their strength and settle old scores — who knows what disaster will follow?

sentences.zh: 今及其謀議未成，宜早圖之。」

translations.literal: Now while their plotting is not yet settled, we should move against them early."
translations.idiomatic: We must strike before their plans take shape."

sentences.zh: 恭以為然，以告殷仲堪、桓玄。

translations.literal: Gong thought this correct and told Yin Zhongkan and Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong agreed and informed Yin Zhongkan and Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 仲堪、玄許之，推恭為盟主，刻期同趣京師。

translations.literal: Zhongkan and Xuan assented; they made Gong alliance leader and set a date to advance on the capital together.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Huan gave their assent, made Wang Gong leader of the alliance, and fixed a day to march on the capital together.

sentences.zh: 時內外疑阻，津邏嚴急，仲堪以斜絹為書，內箭簳中，合鏑漆之，因庾楷以送恭。

translations.literal: At this time suspicion and obstruction prevailed inside and outside; the river crossings were tightly guarded. Zhongkan wrote a letter on diagonal silk, placed it inside an arrow shaft, sealed it with lacquer where the head was joined, and through Yu Kai sent it to Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion gripped court and provinces alike, and river crossings were under tight guard. Yin Zhongkan wrote his message on a strip of slanted silk, hid it inside an arrow shaft, sealed the joint with lacquer, and sent it to Wang Gong by way of Yu Kai.

sentences.zh: 恭發書，絹文角戾，不復能辨仲堪手書，疑楷詐為之，且謂仲堪去年已違期不赴，今必不動，乃先期舉兵。

translations.literal: When Gong opened the letter, the silk writing was distorted and he could no longer tell Zhongkan's hand; he suspected Kai had forged it, and furthermore thought that since Zhongkan had failed to keep last year's agreed date, he would certainly not move now — so he raised troops ahead of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gong opened the message, the writing on the silk had warped and he could no longer recognize Yin Zhongkan's hand. He suspected Yu Kai of forgery and, remembering that Yin had missed last year's deadline, assumed he would not stir this time either — and so moved early with his own army.

sentences.zh: 司馬劉牢之諫曰：「將軍，國之元舅；

translations.literal: The Major Liu Laozhi remonstrated, saying: "General, you are the foremost maternal uncle of the state;
translations.idiomatic: His chief of staff Liu Laozhi urged him: "General, you are the emperor's senior maternal uncle;

sentences.zh: 會稽王，天子叔父也。

translations.literal: the Prince of Kuaiji is the emperor's uncle.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Kuaiji is the emperor's uncle by blood.

sentences.zh: 會稽王又當國秉政，向為將軍戮其所愛王國寶、王緒，又送王廞書，其深伏將軍已多矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji moreover holds the reins of government; earlier, for the General's sake he executed the men he loved, Wang Guobao and Wang Xu, and he also handed over Wang Yin's letter — he has already bowed deeply before the General in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: The prince moreover holds the government in his hands. For your sake he already executed his favorites Wang Guobao and Wang Xu and yielded up Wang Yin's correspondence — he has abased himself before you more than once.

sentences.zh: 頃所援任，雖未允愜，亦非大失。

translations.literal: The recent appointments he supported, though not fully satisfactory, were not a great loss either.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments made at his urging may not have pleased you, but they were hardly a grave injury.

sentences.zh: 割庾楷四郡以配王愉，於將軍何損！

translations.literal: Carving four of Yu Kai's commanderies to assign to Wang Yu — what loss is that to the General!
translations.idiomatic: What harm does it do you to give four of Yu Kai's commanderies to Wang Yu?

sentences.zh: 晉陽之甲，豈可數興乎！」

translations.literal: The hosts of Jinyang — can they be raised repeatedly!"
translations.idiomatic: Armies raised against the capital cannot be summoned again and again!"

sentences.zh: 恭不從，上表請討王愉、司馬尚之兄弟。

translations.literal: Gong did not listen and submitted a memorial requesting punitive action against Wang Yu and the Shangzhi brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong would not be swayed and memorialized the throne to campaign against Wang Yu and Simao Shangzhi and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 道子使人說楷曰；

translations.literal: Daozi sent someone to persuade Kai, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Daozi dispatched an envoy to remonstrate with Yu Kai:

sentences.zh: 「昔我一卿，恩如骨肉，帳中之飲，結帶之言，可謂親矣。

translations.literal: "In the past you and I, my lord, were as close as flesh and bone — drinking in the tent, words bound by our sashes — it could be called intimacy indeed.
translations.idiomatic: "You and I were once as close as kin — sharing wine in the tent, swearing oaths with our sashes tied together. That was true friendship.

sentences.zh: 卿今棄舊交，結新援，忘王恭疇昔陵侮之恥乎！

translations.literal: My lord now abandons the old friendship and forms new alliances — have you forgotten the shame of Wang Gong's past insults and bullying!
translations.idiomatic: Now you cast aside an old ally for new ones — have you forgotten how Wang Gong humiliated you in times past?

sentences.zh: 若欲委體而臣之，使恭得志，必以卿為反覆之人，安肯深相親信！

translations.literal: If you wish to surrender yourself and serve him, once Gong gets his way he will surely regard you as a man who shifts with every wind — how would he deeply trust and be close to you!
translations.idiomatic: If you bow to him and serve his cause, once Gong triumphs he will mark you as a turncoat — why would he ever trust you again?

sentences.zh: 首身且不可保，況富貴乎！」

translations.literal: Even your head and body cannot be preserved — how much less wealth and rank!"
translations.idiomatic: Your life will not be safe, let alone your fortune!"

sentences.zh: 楷怒曰：「王恭昔赴山陵，相王憂懼無計，我知事急，尋勒兵而至，恭不敢發。

translations.literal: Kai angrily said: "When Wang Gong once went to the imperial tombs, the Prince Regent was worried and at his wit's end; knowing the matter was urgent, I soon marshaled troops and arrived — Gong dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai retorted: "When Wang Gong marched on the imperial tombs, the Prince Regent was desperate with fear. I saw the crisis, gathered my troops, and came at once — and Gong did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 去年之事，我亦俟命而動。

translations.literal: In last year's affair I also waited for orders before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Last year as well I waited on his command before I moved.

sentences.zh: 我事相王，無相負者。

translations.literal: In serving the Prince Regent I have never failed him.
translations.idiomatic: In all my service to the Prince Regent, I have never betrayed him.

sentences.zh: 相王不能拒恭，反殺國寶及緒，自爾已來，誰敢復為相王盡力者！

translations.literal: The Prince Regent could not resist Gong but instead killed Guobao and Xu — since then, who would dare exert himself again for the Prince Regent!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Regent could not stand up to Gong, yet killed Guobao and Xu instead — since then, who would still risk everything for him?

sentences.zh: 庾楷實不能以百口助人屠滅。」

translations.literal: Yu Kai truly cannot use the lives of a hundred mouths to help others in slaughter and destruction."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai cannot expose a household of a hundred souls to annihilation for someone else's war."

sentences.zh: 時楷已應恭檄，正征士馬。

translations.literal: At this time Kai had already answered Gong's proclamation and was levying troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yu Kai had already answered Wang Gong's call and was raising troops.

sentences.zh: 信返，朝廷憂懼，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: When the messenger returned, the court was fearful; inside and outside martial law was declared.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned with Kai's answer, the court panicked and declared a general alert.

sentences.zh: 會稽世子元顯言於道子曰：「前不討王恭，故有今日難。

translations.literal: Simao Yuanxian, heir of Kuaiji, said to Daozi: "Because we did not punish Wang Gong before, we have today's crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Simao Yuanxian, heir apparent of Kuaiji, told Daozi: "We brought on today's crisis by failing to crush Wang Gong when we had the chance.

sentences.zh: 今若復從其欲，則太宰之禍至矣。

translations.literal: If we now again yield to their wishes, the Grand Preceptor's calamity will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: If we submit to them again, the Grand Preceptor will share the same fate.

sentences.zh: 道子不知所為，悉以事委元顯，日飲醇酒而已。

translations.literal: Daozi did not know what to do; he entrusted everything to Yuanxian and merely drank strong wine every day.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi, at a loss, handed all affairs to Yuanxian and spent his days in drink.

sentences.zh: 元顯聰警，皮涉文義，志氣果銳，以安危為己任。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was sharp-witted, superficially versed in literary meaning, bold and resolute in spirit, and took the realm's safety as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was quick and clever, with a passing grasp of the classics, a fierce and decisive temperament, and a keen sense that the fate of the realm rested on his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 附會之者，謂元顯神武，有明帝之風。

translations.literal: Those who attached themselves to him said Yuanxian was martial and divine, with the air of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers called him a warrior-sage in the mold of Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪聞恭舉兵，自以去歲後期，乃勒兵趣發。
