translations.literal: Yin Zhongkan heard that Gong had raised troops; thinking of how he had missed the deadline last year, he mustered his army and hurried to march.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhongkan heard that Wang Gong had taken up arms, mindful that he had missed last year's rendezvous, he mobilized and rushed to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 仲堪素不習為將，悉以軍事委南郡相楊佺期兄弟，使佺期帥舟師五千為前鋒，桓玄次之，仲堪帥兵二萬，相繼而下。

translations.literal: Zhongkan had never been accustomed to commanding; he entrusted all military affairs to the Yang Qianqi brothers, Administrators of Nan Commandery — he had Qianqi lead five thousand river troops as vanguard, Huan Xuan next, and Zhongkan himself command twenty thousand men, advancing in successive stages downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan was no natural general. He put the army in the hands of the Yang brothers of Nan Commandery: Qianqi led five thousand river troops as vanguard, Huan Xuan came next, and Yin himself brought twenty thousand men downriver in stages.

sentences.zh: 佺期自以其先漢太尉震至父亮，九世皆以才德著名，矜其門地，謂江左莫及。

translations.literal: Qianqi considered that from his ancestor the Han Grand Commandant Yang Zhen to his father Yang Liang, nine generations were all famed for talent and virtue; he prided himself on his lineage and thought none in the lands east of the Yangzi could match it.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqi traced his line from the Han Grand Commandant Yang Zhen through his father Yang Liang — nine generations celebrated for talent and integrity — and considered his house unmatched in the Jiangzuo elite.

sentences.zh: 有以比王珣者，佺期猶恚恨。

translations.literal: When someone compared him to Wang Xun, Qianqi still nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Even when people likened him to Wang Xun, Qianqi remained bitter.

sentences.zh: 而時流以其晚過江，婚宦失類，佺期及兄廣、弟思平、從弟孜敬皆粗獷，每排抑之。

translations.literal: Yet the men of the age, because they had crossed the river late and their marriages and offices were ill-matched, and because Qianqi together with his elder brother Guang, younger brother Siping, and cousin Zijing were all rough and uncouth, constantly pushed them down.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry, however, looked down on them as latecomers from the north with misaligned marriages and posts, and dismissed Qianqi, his brothers Guang and Siping, and his cousin Zijing as crude men — and snubbed them at every turn.

sentences.zh: 佺期常慷慨切齒，欲因事際以逞其志，故亦贊成仲堪之謀。

translations.literal: Qianqi often spoke with indignant vehemence, grinding his teeth, wishing to seize the occasion to fulfill his ambition — therefore he also supported Zhongkan's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqi burned with humiliated rage and longed for any chance to prove himself — which is why he backed Yin Zhongkan's scheme.

sentences.zh: 八月，佺期、玄奄至湓口。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Qianqi and Xuan suddenly arrived at Pankou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yang Qianqi and Huan Xuan suddenly appeared at Pankou.

sentences.zh: 王愉無備，惶遽奔臨川，玄遣偏軍追獲之。

translations.literal: Wang Yu was unprepared; in panic he fled to Linchuan. Xuan sent a detached force in pursuit and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, caught off guard, fled in panic toward Linchuan. Huan Xuan sent a flanking detachment that ran him down and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 燕以河間公熙為侍中、車騎大將軍、中領軍、司隸校尉，城陽公元為衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yan appointed Murong Xi, Duke of Hejian, to Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army Commander, and Colonel Director of Retainers; Murong Yuan, Duke of Chengyang, to Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan, Murong Xi, Duke of Hejian, was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army Commander, and Colonel Director of Retainers; Murong Yuan, Duke of Chengyang, was made Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元，寶之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan was Bao's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was the son of Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 又以劉忠為左將軍，張豪為後將軍，並賜姓慕容氏。

translations.literal: Liu Zhong was also made General of the Left and Zhang Hao General of the Rear, both granted the surname Murong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong became General of the Left and Zhang Hao General of the Rear, and both received the surname Murong.

sentences.zh: 李旱為中常侍、輔國將軍，衛雙為前將軍，張順為鎮西將軍、昌黎尹，張真為右將軍；

translations.literal: Li Han became Palace Attendant and General Who Stabilizes the State; Wei Shuang, General of the Van; Zhang Shun, General Who Pacifies the West and Magistrate of Changli; Zhang Zhen, General of the Right;
translations.idiomatic: Li Han was made Palace Attendant and General Who Stabilizes the State; Wei Shuang, General of the Van; Zhang Shun, General Who Pacifies the West and Prefect of Changli; and Zhang Zhen, General of the Right;

sentences.zh: 皆封公。

translations.literal: all were enfeoffed as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: all were enfeoffed as dukes.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，燕步兵校尉馬勤等謀反，伏誅；

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Ma Qin, Commandant of Foot Soldiers of Yan, and others plotted rebellion and were executed where they lay;
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, Ma Qin, Infantry Commandant of Yan, and others plotted rebellion and were put to death on the spot;

sentences.zh: 事連驃騎將軍高陽公崇、崇弟東平公澄，皆賜死。

translations.literal: the affair implicated Murong Chong, Duke of Gaoyang and General of Fast Cavalry, and Chong's younger brother Murong Cheng, Duke of Dongping — all were ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: the conspiracy involved Murong Chong, Duke of Gaoyang and General of Fast Cavalry, and his brother Murong Cheng, Duke of Dongping — both were granted death by poison.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將國鄧啟方、南陽太守閭丘羨將兵二萬擊南燕，與南燕中軍將國法、撫軍將軍和戰於管城，啟方等兵敗，單騎走免。

translations.literal: Deng Qifang of Ningshuo and Qiuchi Xian, Administrator of Nanyang, led twenty thousand troops to attack Southern Yan; they fought at Guancheng against Fa and He, Central Army General and Pacifying-Army General of Southern Yan; Qifang and the rest were defeated and escaped alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qifang of Ningshuo and Qiuchi Xian, prefect of Nanyang, marched twenty thousand men against Southern Yan and met Fa and He of that court — Central Army General and Pacifying-Army General — at Guancheng. Deng's force was routed; he fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪命有司正封畿，標道裡，平權衡，審度量；

translations.literal: The King of Wei, Tuoba Gui, ordered the officials to rectify the boundaries of the royal domain, mark road distances, level the balances, and examine measures;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui ordered his officials to fix the domain's boundaries, post distances along the roads, standardize weights, and inspect measures;

sentences.zh: 遣使循行郡國，舉奏守宰不法者，親考察黜陟之。

translations.literal: he sent envoys to tour the commanderies and kingdoms, memorializing unlawful governors and magistrates, and personally inspected and promoted or demoted them.
translations.idiomatic: and sent commissioners through the provinces to report corrupt officials and personally review promotions and dismissals.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛卯，加會稽王道子黃鉞，以世子元顯為征討都督，遣衛將軍王珣、右將軍謝琰將兵討王恭，譙王尚之將兵討庾楷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinmao, Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, was given the yellow battle-axe; Yuanxian the heir was made Commander-in-Chief for Punitive Campaigns; Defender-in-Chief Wang Xun and General of the Right Xie Yan were sent with troops to punish Wang Gong; Prince of Qiao Simao Shangzhi was sent with troops to punish Yu Kai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day xinmao, Simao Daozi received the yellow battle-axe of supreme command. His heir Yuanxian was named Grand Commander for the punitive campaign. Wang Xun, Defender-in-Chief, and Xie Yan, General of the Right, were dispatched against Wang Gong; Simao Shangzhi, Prince of Qiao, against Yu Kai.

sentences.zh: 乙未，燕以東陽公根為尚書令，張通為左僕射，衛倫為右僕射，慕容豪為幽州刺史，鎮肥如。

translations.literal: On the day yimi, Yan appointed Murong Gen, Duke of Dongyang, Master of Writing; Zhang Tong, Left Vice Director; Wei Lun, Right Vice Director; Murong Hao, Inspector of You Province, garrisoning Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimi, Yan made Murong Gen, Duke of Dongyang, head of the Masters of Writing; Zhang Tong and Wei Lun its left and right vice directors; and Murong Hao Inspector of You, stationed at Feiru.

sentences.zh: 己亥，譙王尚之大破庾楷於牛渚，楷單騎奔桓玄。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Prince of Qiao Simao Shangzhi routed Yu Kai at Niuzhu; Kai fled alone on horseback to Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jihai, Simao Shangzhi crushed Yu Kai at Niuzhu. Kai escaped alone to join Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子以尚之為豫州刺史，弟恢之為驃騎司馬、丹楊尹，允之為吳國內史，休之為襄城太守，各擁兵馬以為己援。

translations.literal: Simao Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, made Shangzhi Inspector of Yu Province; his younger brother Huizhi, Chief Clerk to the Fast Cavalry General and Magistrate of Danyang; Yunzhi, Administrator of the Wu Principality; and Xiuzhi, Administrator of Xiangcheng — each holding troops and horses as his own support.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi made Shangzhi Inspector of Yu and gave his brothers their own commands: Huizhi as chief clerk to the Fast Cavalry General and magistrate of Danyang; Yunzhi as administrator of Wu; Xiuzhi as prefect of Xiangcheng — each with military forces to serve as Daozi's private backing.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，桓玄大破官軍於白石。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, Huan Xuan heavily defeated the imperial army at Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, Huan Xuan routed the court army at Baishi.

sentences.zh: 玄與楊佺期進至橫江，尚之退走，恢之所領水軍皆沒。

translations.literal: Xuan and Yang Qianqi advanced to Hengjiang; Shangzhi retreated; Huizhi's river troops were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan and Yang Qianqi pushed to Hengjiang. Shangzhi fell back, and Huizhi's entire flotilla was lost.

sentences.zh: 丙午，道子屯中堂，元顯守石頭，己酉，王珣守北郊，謝琰屯宣陽門，以備之。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Daozi encamped at Zhongtang; Yuanxian guarded Shitou; on the day jiyou, Wang Xun guarded the northern suburbs; Xie Yan encamped at Xuanyang Gate — all to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu Daozi took station at Zhongtang and Yuanxian held Shitou; on jiyou Wang Xun guarded the northern suburbs and Xie Yan the Xuanyang Gate — all bracing for the rebel advance.

sentences.zh: 王恭素以才地陵物，既殺王國寶，自謂威無不行，仗劉牢之為爪牙而但以部曲將遇之，牢之負其才，深懷恥恨。

translations.literal: Wang Gong had always looked down on others with his talent and status; after killing Wang Guobao he considered his authority unstoppable; he relied on Liu Laozhi as his claws and fangs but treated him only as a staff general — Laozhi, proud of his ability, nursed deep shame and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong had always lorded his talent and birth over others. After the killing of Wang Guobao he believed his word was law. He leaned on Liu Laozhi as his enforcer yet treated him like a mere troop captain. Laozhi, confident in his own worth, seethed with humiliation.

sentences.zh: 元顯知之，遣廬江太守高素說牢之，使叛恭，許事成即以恭位號授之；

translations.literal: Yuanxian learned of this and sent Gao Su, Administrator of Lujiang, to persuade Laozhi to betray Gong, promising that once the affair succeeded he would give him Gong's title and position;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian saw his opening and sent Gao Su, prefect of Lujiang, to tempt Laozhi into betraying Wang Gong, promising him Gong's titles once the coup succeeded;

sentences.zh: 又以道子書遺牢之，為陳禍福。

translations.literal: he also sent Daozi's letter to Laozhi, setting forth fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: and forwarded a letter from Daozi laying out the stakes.

sentences.zh: 牢子謂其子敬宣曰；

translations.literal: Laozhi said to his son Jingxuan:
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi said to his son Jingxuan:

sentences.zh: 「王恭昔受先帝大恩，今為帝舅，不能翼戴王室，數舉兵向京師，吾不能審恭之志，事捷之日，必能為天子相王之下乎？

translations.literal: "Wang Gong once received great favor from the late emperor; now he is the emperor's uncle, yet he cannot support and uphold the royal house and has repeatedly raised troops against the capital — I cannot discern Gong's intentions; on the day of success, can he truly remain below the emperor and the Prince Regent?
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Gong enjoyed the late emperor's deepest trust and is now the emperor's uncle. Instead of shielding the throne he keeps marching on the capital. I cannot read his mind — if he wins, will he truly stop short of ruling the emperor and the Prince Regent?

sentences.zh: 吾欲奉國威靈，以順討逆，何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to uphold the nation's authority and majesty and, in accordance with righteousness, punish the rebel — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to serve the throne and punish rebellion in the name of the state. What say you?"

sentences.zh: 敬宣曰：「朝廷雖無成、康之美，亦無幽、厲之惡；

translations.literal: Jingxuan said: "Although the court lacks the excellence of Cheng and Kang, it also lacks the wickedness of You and Li;
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan replied: "The court is no golden age of Cheng and Kang, but neither is it the tyranny of You and Li;

sentences.zh: 而恭恃其兵威，暴蔑王室。

translations.literal: yet Gong relies on his military might and treats the royal house with violence and contempt.
translations.idiomatic: yet Gong abuses his arms to insult the throne.

sentences.zh: 大人親非骨肉，義非君臣，雖共事少時，意好不協，今日討之，於情義何有！」

translations.literal: My lord is not related by blood, nor bound as minister and sovereign; though you served together briefly and your inclinations did not harmonize, to punish him today — what violation of feeling and duty is there!"
translations.idiomatic: You are neither kin nor true liege and subject. You worked together only briefly and never liked each other — where is the breach of loyalty in striking him down now?"

sentences.zh: 恭參軍何澹之知其謀，以告恭。

translations.literal: Wang Gong's aide He Tanzhi learned of the plot and told Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He Tanzhi, an officer on Wang Gong's staff, learned of the plot and informed Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭以澹之素與牢之有隙，不信。

translations.literal: Gong, because Tanzhi had long been at odds with Laozhi, did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong, knowing Tanzhi's old feud with Laozhi, refused to believe him.

sentences.zh: 乃置酒請牢之，於眾中拜之為兄，精兵堅甲，悉以配之，使帥帳下督顏延為前鋒。

translations.literal: He then set out wine and invited Laozhi; before the assembly he bowed to him as elder brother; elite troops and strong armor he gave entirely to him; he had him lead his personal guard supervisor Yan Yan as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he held a feast for Laozhi, hailed him before the whole camp as an elder brother, and entrusted him with his best troops and armor, with Yan Yan leading the vanguard under his command.

sentences.zh: 牢之至竹裡，斬延以降；

translations.literal: Laozhi reached Zhuli, beheaded Yan and surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuli, Laozhi killed Yan Yan and went over to the court;

sentences.zh: 遣敬宣及其婿東莞太守高雅之還襲恭。

translations.literal: he sent Jingxuan and his son-in-law Gao Yazhi, Administrator of Dongguan, back to strike Gong by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: then sent Jingxuan and his son-in-law Gao Yazhi, prefect of Dongguan, to turn on Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭方出城曜兵，敬宣縱騎橫擊之，恭兵皆潰。

translations.literal: Gong had just gone out of the city to display his troops; Jingxuan unleashed horsemen in a flanking attack; Gong's soldiers all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong was reviewing his troops outside the walls when Jingxuan hit him with a cavalry charge. Gong's army broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 恭將入城，雅之已閉城門。

translations.literal: As Gong was about to enter the city, Yazhi had already closed the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong raced for the gate, Yazhi had already barred it.

sentences.zh: 恭單騎奔曲阿，素不習馬，髀中生瘡。

translations.literal: Gong fled alone on horseback to Qu'e; unaccustomed to riding, sores formed on his buttocks.
translations.idiomatic: Gong fled alone toward Qu'e. Unused to the saddle, he rubbed raw sores on his thighs.

sentences.zh: 曲阿人殷確，恭故吏也，以船載恭，將奔桓玄，至長塘湖，為人所告，獲之，送京師，斬於倪塘。

translations.literal: Yin Que of Qu'e, a former subordinate of Gong's, carried Gong by boat, intending to flee to Huan Xuan; at Changtang Lake he was reported by someone, captured, sent to the capital, and beheaded at Nitang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Que, a former retainer of Gong's from Qu'e, hid him in a boat bound for Huan Xuan's lines. At Changtang Lake someone informed on them; Gong was seized, sent to the capital, and executed at Nitang.

sentences.zh: 恭臨刑，猶理鬚鬢，神色自若，謂臨刑者曰：「我暗於信人，所以至此，原其本心，豈不忠於社稷邪！

translations.literal: At execution Gong still arranged his beard and sideburns, his expression calm; he said to the executioners: "I was blind in trusting others, and so came to this — consider my original heart: was I not loyal to the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: At the block Wang Gong still combed his beard, serene as ever. He told the executioners: "I was a poor judge of men, and that brought me here — but judge my intent: was I not loyal to the realm?

sentences.zh: 但令百世之下知有王恭耳。」

translations.literal: Only let those a hundred generations hence know there was a Wang Gong."
translations.idiomatic: Let only posterity remember that Wang Gong lived."

sentences.zh: 並其子弟黨與皆死。

translations.literal: His sons, younger brothers, and partisans all died.
translations.idiomatic: His kin and followers were put to death with him.

sentences.zh: 以劉牢之為都督兗、表、冀、幽、并、徐、揚州、晉陵諸軍事以代恭。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi was made Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Yan, Biao, Ji, You, Bing, Xu, Yang, and Jinling to replace Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi was appointed commander over Yan, Biao, Ji, You, Bing, Xu, Yang, and Jinling in Wang Gong's place.

sentences.zh: 俄而楊佺期、桓玄至石頭，殷仲堪至蕪湖。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Qianqi and Huan Xuan reached Shitou; Yin Zhongkan reached Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yang Qianqi and Huan Xuan arrived at Shitou and Yin Zhongkan at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 元顯自竹裡馳還京師，遣丹楊尹王愷等發京邑士民數萬人據石頭以拒之。

translations.literal: Yuanxian raced back from Zhuli to the capital; he sent Wang Kai, Magistrate of Danyang, and others to mobilize tens of thousands of capital gentlemen and commoners to hold Shitou and resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian galloped back from Zhuli and sent Wang Kai, magistrate of Danyang, to rally tens of thousands of townspeople to hold Shitou against them.

sentences.zh: 佺期、玄等上表理王恭，求誅劉牢之。

translations.literal: Qianqi, Xuan, and the rest submitted memorials vindicating Wang Gong and requesting Liu Laozhi's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqi and Huan Xuan memorialized the throne to clear Wang Gong's name and demand Liu Laozhi's death.

sentences.zh: 牢之帥北府之眾馳赴京師，軍於新亭。

translations.literal: Laozhi led the Northern Headquarters host in a dash to the capital and encamped at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi marched the Northern Headquarters army posthaste to the capital and camped at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 佺期、玄見之失色，回軍蔡洲。

translations.literal: Qianqi and Xuan, seeing this, turned pale; they withdrew their army to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the sight of Laozhi's host, Qianqi and Huan Xuan lost their color and pulled back to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷未知西軍虛實，仲堪等擁眾數萬，充斥郊畿，內外憂逼。

translations.literal: The court did not yet know the true state of the western army; Zhongkan and the rest held armies numbering tens of thousands, filling the capital outskirts — inside and outside all were pressed with anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: The court still could not gauge the western army's strength. Yin Zhongkan's tens of thousands packed the capital's outskirts, and fear gripped city and palace alike.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍桓修，沖之子也，言於道子曰：「西軍可說而解也，修知其情矣。

translations.literal: Huan Xiu, General of the Left Guard and son of Huan Chong, said to Daozi: "The western army can be persuaded and dispersed — Xiu knows their minds.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiu, Left Guard General and son of Huan Chong, told Daozi: "The western force can be talked apart — I know how they think.

sentences.zh: 殷、桓之下，專恃王恭，恭既破滅，西軍沮恐。

translations.literal: Under Yin and Huan they relied solely on Wang Gong; now that Gong is destroyed, the western army is dejected and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Huan counted on Wang Gong alone. With him gone, their army is demoralized.

sentences.zh: 今若以重利啖玄及佺期，二人必內喜；

translations.literal: If heavy rewards are now used to entice Xuan and Qianqi, the two will surely rejoice inwardly;
translations.idiomatic: Offer Huan Xuan and Yang Qianqi rich rewards and both will jump at them inwardly;

sentences.zh: 玄能制仲堪，佺期可使倒戈，取仲堪矣。」

translations.literal: Xuan can control Zhongkan; Qianqi can be made to turn his blades — then Zhongkan can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan can hold Yin Zhongkan in check, and Qianqi can be turned to strike him down."

sentences.zh: 道子納之，以玄為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Daozi accepted this and made Xuan Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi took the advice and made Huan Xuan Inspector of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 召郗恢為尚書，以佺期代恢為都督梁、雍、秦三州諸軍事、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Chi Hui was recalled as Master of Writing; Qianqi replaced Hui as Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Liang, Yong, and Qin and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Hui was recalled to the Masters of Writing, and Qianqi replaced him as commander of Liang, Yong, and Qin and Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 以修為荊州刺史，權領左衛文武之鎮，又令劉牢之以千人送之。

translations.literal: Xiu was made Inspector of Jing Province, exercising in proxy the civil and military garrison of the Left Guard; Liu Laozhi was also ordered to escort him with a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiu became Inspector of Jing and acting commander of the Left Guard garrison, with a thousand of Liu Laozhi's men as escort.

sentences.zh: 黜仲堪為廣州刺史，遣仲堪叔父太常茂宣詔，敕仲堪回軍。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was demoted to Inspector of Guang Province; his uncle Mao, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was sent to proclaim the edict ordering Zhongkan to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan was demoted to Inspector of Guang, and his uncle Mao, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was sent with an edict ordering him home.

sentences.zh: 張驤子超收合三千餘家據南皮，自號烏桓王，抄掠諸郡。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao, son of Zhang Qiang, gathered more than three thousand households, seized Nanpi, styled himself King of the Wuhuan, and raided the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao, son of Zhang Qiang, mustered more than three thousand households, seized Nanpi, proclaimed himself King of the Wuhuan, and plundered the surrounding commanderies.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪命庾岳討之。

translations.literal: Tuoba Gui, King of Wei, ordered Yu Yue to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui, King of Wei, sent Yu Yue to put them down.

sentences.zh: 楊軌屯廉川，收集夷、夏，眾至萬餘。

translations.literal: Yang Gui encamped at Lianchuan, gathered Yi and Han peoples, and his followers reached more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui held Lianchuan, rallied both tribal and Chinese followers, and mustered more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 王乞基謂軌曰：「禿髮氏才高而兵盛，且乞基之主也，不如歸之。」

translations.literal: Wang Qiji said to Gui, "The Tufa clan is talented and their troops are strong, and moreover they are Qiji's masters — better to submit to them."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiji told Yang Gui, "The Tufa are able commanders with a strong army, and they are my lords besides. We would do better to join them."

sentences.zh: 軌乃遣使降於西平王烏孤。

translations.literal: Gui then sent envoys to surrender to Tufa Wugu, King of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui sent envoys to submit to Tufa Wugu, King of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 軌尋為羌酋梁饑所敗，西奔人零海，襲乙弗鮮卑而據其地。

translations.literal: Before long Gui was defeated by the Qiang chieftain Liang Ji; he fled west into Linghai, attacked the Yifu Xianbei, and seized their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yang Gui was routed by the Qiang chieftain Liang Ji. He fled west into Linghai, fell upon the Yifu Xianbei, and took their lands.

sentences.zh: 烏孤謂群臣曰：「楊軌、□乞基歸誠於我，卿等不速救，使為羌人所覆，孤甚愧之。」

translations.literal: Wugu said to his ministers, "Yang Gui and Wang Qiji came over to me in good faith, yet you did not hurry to rescue them and let them be overrun by the Qiang — I am deeply ashamed of this."
translations.idiomatic: Wugu told his court, "Yang Gui and Wang Qiji pledged themselves to me, yet you failed to rescue them in time and let the Qiang destroy them. I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 平西將軍渾屯曰：「梁饑無經遠大略，可一戰擒也。」

translations.literal: Hun Tun, General Who Pacifies the West, said, "Liang Ji has no long-range grand strategy — he can be captured in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: Hun Tun, the Pacifier of the West, said, "Liang Ji lacks any far-sighted plan. One battle will be enough to take him."

sentences.zh: 饑進攻西平，西平人田玄明執太守郭幸而代之，以拒饑，遣子為質於烏孤。

translations.literal: Ji advanced to attack Xiping; Tian Xuanming of Xiping seized the Administrator Guo Xing, replaced him, resisted Ji, and sent his son as hostage to Wugu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ji marched on Xiping. Tian Xuanming of that city arrested the prefect Guo Xing, took his place, and held Ji at bay, sending his son to Wugu as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 烏孤欲救之，群臣憚饑兵強，多以為疑。

translations.literal: Wugu wished to rescue them, but the ministers feared Ji's strong army and mostly expressed doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu wanted to go to their aid, but his ministers feared Liang Ji's strength and mostly urged caution.

sentences.zh: 左司馬趙振曰：「楊軌新敗，呂氏方強，洪池以北，未可冀也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhen, Left Major, said, "Yang Gui has just been defeated, the Lü clan is at the height of its power, and north of Hongchi there is nothing to hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhen, the left major, said, "Yang Gui has just been beaten, the Lü are at their peak, and nothing north of Hongchi is within reach.

sentences.zh: 嶺南五郡，庶幾可取。

translations.literal: The five commanderies south of the mountains may perhaps be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The five commanderies south of the mountains, however, might yet be ours.

sentences.zh: 大王若無開拓之志，振不敢言；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty has no ambition to expand, Zhen dares not speak further;
translations.idiomatic: If you have no mind to expand our domain, I have nothing more to say;

sentences.zh: 若欲經營四方，此機不可失也。

translations.literal: if you wish to manage affairs in all directions, this opportunity must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: but if you mean to build an empire in every quarter, this chance will not come again.

sentences.zh: 使羌得西平，華、夷震動，非我之利也。」

translations.literal: If the Qiang take Xiping, Chinese and barbarians alike will be shaken — this is not to our advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Qiang hold Xiping and every Chinese and tribal power will tremble. That does us no good."

sentences.zh: 烏孤喜曰：「吾亦欲乘時立功，安能坐守窮谷乎！」

translations.literal: Wugu said with pleasure, "I too wish to seize the moment and win merit — how can I sit guarding a wretched valley!"
translations.idiomatic: Wugu was delighted. "I mean to seize this moment and make my mark. How can I sit forever in this wretched gorge!"

sentences.zh: 乃謂群臣曰：「梁饑若得西平，保據山河，不可複製。

translations.literal: He then told his ministers, "If Liang Ji takes Xiping and holds fast to its mountains and rivers, he cannot be brought under control again.
translations.idiomatic: He told the court, "If Liang Ji takes Xiping and holds its mountains and rivers, we will never bring him to heel again.

sentences.zh: 饑雖驍猛，軍令不整，易破也。」

translations.literal: Although Ji is fierce and bold, his army's discipline is not tight — he is easy to break."
translations.idiomatic: Ji is fierce, but his troops are undisciplined. They will break easily."

sentences.zh: 遂進擊饑，大破之。

translations.literal: He then advanced to attack Ji and inflicted a great defeat on him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Liang Ji and routed him.

sentences.zh: 饑退屯龍支堡。

translations.literal: Ji withdrew and encamped at Longzhi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ji fell back to Longzhi Fort.

sentences.zh: 烏孤進攻，拔之，饑單騎奔澆河，俘斬數萬，以田玄明為四平內史。

translations.literal: Wugu pressed the attack, took the fort, and Ji fled alone on horseback to Jiaohe; tens of thousands were captured or killed, and Tian Xuanming was made Inner Secretary of Siping.
translations.idiomatic: Wugu stormed the fort and took it. Liang Ji escaped alone to Jiaohe. Tens of thousands were killed or captured, and Tian Xuanming was made administrator of Siping.

sentences.zh: 樂都太守田瑤、湟河太守張裯、澆河太守王稚皆以郡降，嶺南羌、胡數萬落皆附於烏孤。

translations.literal: Tian Yao, Administrator of Ledu; Zhang Chou, Administrator of Huanghe; and Wang Zhi, Administrator of Jiaohe, all surrendered their commanderies; several tens of thousands of Qiang and Hu households south of the mountains all attached themselves to Wugu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yao of Ledu, Zhang Chou of Huanghe, and Wang Zhi of Jiaohe all surrendered their commanderies. Several tens of thousands of Qiang and Hu households south of the mountains submitted to Wugu.

sentences.zh: 西秦王乾是遣秦州牧益州、武衛將軍慕兀、冠軍將軍翟瑁帥騎二萬伐吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, King of Western Qin, sent Qifu Yizhou, Governor of Qin Province, Mu Wu, General of the Martial Guard, and Zhai Mao, General Who Wins Every Battle, leading twenty thousand horsemen to attack Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui of Western Qin sent Qifu Yizhou, governor of Qin, along with Mu Wu, the martial guard general, and Zhai Mao, the champion general, at the head of twenty thousand cavalry against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸酉，燕群臣復上尊號，丙子，長樂王盛始即皇帝位，大赦，尊皇后段氏曰皇太后，太妃丁氏曰獻莊皇后。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day guiyou the ministers of Yan again offered him a supreme title; on day bingzi Murong Sheng, Prince of Changle, first ascended the imperial throne, declared a general amnesty, honored Empress Duan as Empress Dowager, and honored the Consort Dowager Lady Ding as Empress Xianzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on guiyou day the Yan ministers once more pressed a supreme title upon their ruler. On bingzi day Murong Sheng of Changle took the throne, declared a general amnesty, raised Empress Duan to empress dowager, and made Consort Dowager Lady Ding empress with the title Xianzhuang.

sentences.zh: 初，蘭汗之當國也，盛從燕主寶出亡，蘭妃奉事丁後愈謹。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lanhan held power, Sheng fled into exile with the Yan ruler Murong Bao; the Lan consort served Empress Dowager Ding with ever greater care.
translations.idiomatic: When Lanhan had held the state, Sheng had fled with Murong Bao. The Lan consort had served Empress Dowager Ding with redoubled devotion.

sentences.zh: 及汗誅，盛以妃當從坐，欲殺之；

translations.literal: When Han was executed, Sheng held that the consort should share guilt as an accomplice and wished to kill her;
translations.idiomatic: After Lanhan was put to death, Sheng judged the consort guilty by association and meant to kill her;

sentences.zh: 丁後以妃有保全之功，固爭之，得免，然終不為後。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ding, because the consort had the merit of preserving her life, argued forcefully on her behalf, and she was spared — yet in the end she was never made empress.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ding pleaded that the consort had saved her life and would not let the matter rest. The woman was spared, but she was never raised to empress.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 殷仲堪得詔書，大怒，趣桓玄、楊佺期進軍。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongkan received the imperial edict, was greatly angered, and urged Huan Xuan and Yang Qianqi to advance their armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhongkan received the edict he was furious and ordered Huan Xuan and Yang Qianqi to march.

sentences.zh: 玄等喜於朝命，欲受之，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Xuan and the others were pleased with the court's order and wished to accept it, but hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan and his allies welcomed the court's summons and were inclined to obey, but they wavered.

sentences.zh: 仲堪聞之，遽自蕪湖南歸，遣使告諭蔡洲軍士曰：「汝輩不各自散歸，吾至江陵，盡誅汝餘口。

translations.literal: When Zhongkan heard of this, he hurried back south from Wuhu and sent a messenger to announce to the soldiers of Cai Prefecture, "If you do not each disperse and return home, when I reach Jiangling I will execute every remaining member of your families.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan heard of it and raced back south from Wuhu. He sent word to the troops at Cai Prefecture: "Unless you disband and go home at once, when I reach Jiangling I will kill every one of your families left behind.

sentences.zh: 佺期部將劉系帥二千人先歸。

translations.literal: Liu Xi, a subordinate general of Qianqi, led two thousand men back first.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi, a commander under Qianqi, withdrew first with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 玄等大懼，狼狽西還，追仲堪至尋陽，及之。

translations.literal: Xuan and the others were greatly afraid; in disarray they fled west, pursued Zhongkan as far as Xunyang, and caught up with him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan and his allies were terrified. They fled west in disorder, caught up with Zhongkan at Xunyang, and overtook him.

sentences.zh: 仲堪既失職，倚玄等為援，玄等亦資仲堪兵，雖內相疑阻，勢不得不合。

translations.literal: Zhongkan, having lost his post, relied on Xuan and the others as support; Xuan and the others also needed Zhongkan's troops — although inwardly they distrusted and obstructed one another, the situation forced them to unite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan, stripped of office, needed Huan Xuan's support, and Huan Xuan needed Zhongkan's troops. Though they mistrusted one another, circumstances forced them together.

sentences.zh: 乃以子弟交質，壬午，盟於尋陽，俱不受朝命，連名上疏申理王恭，求誅劉牢之及譙王尚之，並訴仲堪無罪，獨被降黜。

translations.literal: They therefore exchanged sons as hostages; on day renwu they allied at Xunyang, jointly refused the court's orders, and submitted a joint memorial in Wang Gong's defense, requesting the execution of Liu Laozhi and Sima Shangzhi, Prince of Qiao, while also pleading that Zhongkan was innocent and had alone been demoted.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged sons as hostages. On renwu day they swore alliance at Xunyang, rejected the court's orders together, and submitted a joint petition defending Wang Gong, demanding the deaths of Liu Laozhi and Prince Shangzhi of Qiao, and protesting that Zhongkan alone had been punished without cause.

sentences.zh: 朝廷深憚之，內外騷然。

translations.literal: The court deeply feared them, and there was turmoil within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The court was deeply alarmed, and the realm was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 乃復罷桓修，以荊州還仲堪，優詔慰諭，以求和解，仲堪等乃受詔。

translations.literal: The court then again removed Huan Xiu, restored Jing Province to Zhongkan, and sent a gracious edict of consolation and instruction seeking reconciliation; Zhongkan and the others then accepted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The court removed Huan Xiu, restored Jing Province to Zhongkan, and sent a conciliatory edict. At that Zhongkan and his allies accepted the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞江績劾奏桓修專為身計，疑誤朝廷，詔免修官。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji, Inspector-in-Chief of the Censorate, impeached Huan Xiu for scheming solely for his own advantage and misleading the court; an edict removed Xiu from office.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, chief inspector of the censorate, impeached Huan Xiu for serving his own interests and misleading the court. An edict stripped Xiu of his post.

sentences.zh: 初，桓玄在荊州，所為豪縱。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Xuan was in Jing Province, his conduct was overbearing and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan had held Jing Province, his conduct had been arrogant and lawless.

sentences.zh: 仲堪親黨皆勸仲堪殺之，仲堪不聽。

translations.literal: All of Zhongkan's close associates urged him to kill Xuan, but Zhongkan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan's intimates all urged him to kill Huan Xuan, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 及在尋陽，資其聲地，推玄為盟主，玄愈自矜倨。

translations.literal: When they were at Xunyang, Zhongkan relied on Xuan's reputation and territory and promoted Xuan as leader of the alliance; Xuan became ever more proud and haughty.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang, Zhongkan leaned on Huan Xuan's prestige and domain and made him head of the alliance. Huan Xuan grew prouder than ever.

sentences.zh: 楊佺期為人驕悍，玄每以寒士裁之。

translations.literal: Yang Qianqi was by nature proud and fierce; Xuan always treated him as a humble-born scholar and kept him in check.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qianqi was proud and violent by nature, and Huan Xuan constantly put him down as a man of low birth.

sentences.zh: 佺期甚恨，密說仲堪以玄終為患，請於壇所襲之。

translations.literal: Qianqi hated this deeply; in secret he urged Zhongkan that Xuan would ultimately become a threat and asked to attack him at the place of alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqi hated this and secretly urged Zhongkan that Huan Xuan would prove a lasting menace, proposing to strike him at the altar where they had sworn alliance.

sentences.zh: 仲堪忌佺期兄弟勇健，恐既殺玄，不可複製，苦禁之。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was wary of the Qianqi brothers' courage and strength; fearing that once Xuan was killed they could not be controlled, he strictly forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan feared the Qianqi brothers' martial prowess and worried that once Huan Xuan was dead he could not control them. He forbade the plot outright.

sentences.zh: 於是各還所鎮。

translations.literal: Thereupon each returned to his own post.
translations.idiomatic: Each man then returned to his own command.

sentences.zh: 玄亦知佺期之謀，陰有取佺期之志，乃屯於夏口，引始安太守濟陰卞范之為長史以為謀主。

translations.literal: Xuan also knew of Qianqi's plot and secretly resolved to eliminate Qianqi; he then encamped at Xiakou and brought in Bian Fanzhi of Jiyin, Administrator of Shian, as Chief Clerk to serve as his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan learned of the plot and secretly resolved to destroy Qianqi. He encamped at Xiakou and took Bian Fanzhi of Jiyin, prefect of Shian, as his chief clerk and chief adviser.

sentences.zh: 是時，詔書獨不赦庾楷，玄以楷為武昌太守。

translations.literal: At this time the edict of amnesty alone did not pardon Yu Kai; Xuan made Kai Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty edict alone excluded Yu Kai. Huan Xuan appointed him prefect of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 初，郗恢為朝廷拒西軍，玄未得江州，欲奪恢雍州，以恢為廣州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chi Hui had resisted the western armies on the court's behalf; Xuan had not yet obtained Jiang Province and wished to seize Hui's Yong Province, appointing Hui to Guang Province instead.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Hui had held the western armies at bay for the court. Huan Xuan, still without Jiang Province, meant to take Yong from him and reassign him to Guang.

sentences.zh: 恢聞之，懼，詢於眾，眾皆曰：「楊佺期來者，誰不戮力；

translations.literal: When Hui heard this he was afraid; he asked the assembly, and all said, "If Yang Qianqi comes, who will not exert his strength;
translations.idiomatic: Chi Hui was alarmed and asked his officers. They said, "If Yang Qianqi comes, every man will fight to the last;

sentences.zh: 若桓玄來，恐難與為敵。」

translations.literal: if Huan Xuan comes, I fear he will be hard to match as an enemy."
translations.idiomatic: but if Huan Xuan comes, I doubt we can stand against him."

sentences.zh: 既而聞佺期代己，乃與閭丘羨謀阻兵拒之。

translations.literal: Before long, hearing that Qianqi was replacing him, he plotted with Lüqiu Xian to raise troops and resist.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, learning that Qianqi was to replace him, he joined Lüqiu Xian in plotting armed resistance.

sentences.zh: 佺期聞之，聲言玄來入沔，以佺期為前驅。

translations.literal: When Qianqi heard of this, he spread word that Xuan was coming by way of the Mian River and that Qianqi himself was the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqi heard of it and spread word that Huan Xuan was advancing up the Mian with Qianqi in the van.

sentences.zh: 恢眾信之，望風皆潰，恢請降。

translations.literal: Hui's troops believed it; at the mere rumor they all collapsed, and Hui requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Hui's men believed him. They broke and fled at the rumor, and Chi Hui asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 佺期入府，斬閭丘羨，放恢還都，至楊口，殷仲堪陰使人殺之，及其四子，託言群蠻所殺。

translations.literal: Qianqi entered the headquarters, executed Lüqiu Xian, released Hui to return to the capital; at Yangkou, Yin Zhongkan secretly sent men to kill him and his four sons, claiming they had been killed by tribal rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqi entered the headquarters, killed Lüqiu Xian, and let Chi Hui go home. At Yangkou, Yin Zhongkan secretly had him and his four sons murdered, then claimed that tribal rebels had done it.

sentences.zh: 西秦乞伏益州與吐谷渾王視羆戰於度周川，視羆大敗，走保白蘭山，遣子宕豈為質於西秦以請和，西秦王乾歸以宗女妻之。

translations.literal: Qifu Yizhou of Western Qin fought Shipi, King of Tuyuhun, at the Duzhou River; Shipi was greatly defeated, fled to hold Mount Bailan, sent his son Dangqi as hostage to Western Qin to sue for peace, and Qifu Gangui, King of Western Qin, gave him a clanswoman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Yizhou of Western Qin fought Shipi of Tuyuhun at the Duzhou River and routed him. Shipi fled to Mount Bailan, sent his son Dangqi to Western Qin as a hostage to sue for peace, and Qifu Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage.

sentences.zh: 涼建武將軍李鸞以興城降於禿髮烏孤。

translations.literal: Li Luan, General Who Establishes Martial Power of Liang, surrendered Xingcheng to Tufa Wugu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Luan, the Establishing-Martial general of Liang, surrendered Xingcheng to Tufa Wugu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以琅邪王德文為衛將軍、開府儀同三司，征虜將軍元顯為中領軍，領軍將軍王雅為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Sima Dewen, Prince of Langye, was made General of the Guard with the Grand Prefectural Establishment and Equal Honor to the Three Excellencies; Yuan Xian, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was made Central Army Commander; and Wang Ya, Army Commander, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Sima Dewen of Langye became Guard General with an imperial secretariat and honors equal to the Three Excellencies; Yuan Xian, the barbarian-conquering general, became central army commander; and Wang Ya, the army commander, became left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏王珪命尚書吏部郎鄧淵立官制，協音律，儀曹郎清河董謐制禮儀，三公郎王德定律令，太史令晁崇考天象，吏部尚書崔宏總而裁之，以為永式。

translations.literal: On day xinhai Tuoba Gui, King of Wei, ordered Deng Yuan, Director of the Masters of Writing in the Ministry of Personnel, to establish the official system and harmonize musical pitch; Dong Mi of Qinghe, Attendant of the Ceremonial Office, to devise ritual; Wang De, Attendant of the Three Excellencies, to set laws and ordinances; Chao Chong, Director of Astronomy, to examine celestial signs; and Cui Hong, Minister of Personnel, to oversee and adjudicate the whole as permanent standards.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Tuoba Gui ordered Deng Yuan of the personnel directorate to establish the official system and harmonize pitch, Dong Mi of Qinghe of the ceremonial office to draft ritual, Wang De of the three excellencies office to codify law, Chao Chong the grand astrologer to chart the heavens, and Cui Hong the minister of personnel to supervise the whole as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 淵，羌之孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan was a grandson of the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuan was descended from the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 楊軌、王氣基帥戶數千自歸於西平王烏孤。

translations.literal: Yang Gui and Wang Qiji led several thousand households to submit of their own accord to Tufa Wugu, King of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gui and Wang Qiji brought several thousand households and submitted to Tufa Wugu, King of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己丑，魏王基珪即皇帝位，大赦，改元天興。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day jichou Tuoba Gui, King of Wei, ascended the imperial throne, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Tianxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jichou day, Tuoba Gui took the Wei throne, declared a general amnesty, and proclaimed the Tianxing era.

sentences.zh: 命朝野皆束髮加帽；

translations.literal: He ordered that throughout court and country all should bind their hair and wear caps;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered court and country alike to bind their hair and wear caps;

sentences.zh: 追尊遠祖毛以下二十七人皆為皇帝；

translations.literal: he posthumously honored his remote ancestor Mao and the twenty-seven generations below him all as emperors;
translations.idiomatic: posthumously raised his remote ancestor Mao and twenty-six generations after him to the rank of emperor;

sentences.zh: 謚六世祖力微曰神元皇帝，廟號始祖；

translations.literal: he gave his sixth-generation ancestor Liwei the posthumous title Emperor Shenyuan, with temple name Shizu;
translations.idiomatic: gave his sixth-generation ancestor Liwei the posthumous title Emperor Shenyuan and the temple name Founding Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 祖什翼犍曰昭成皇帝；

translations.literal: his ancestor Shiyijian the posthumous title Emperor Zhaocheng;
translations.idiomatic: he named his ancestor Shiyijian Emperor Zhaocheng;

sentences.zh: 廟號高祖；

translations.literal: with temple name Gaozu;
translations.idiomatic: and gave him the temple name High Ancestor;

sentences.zh: 父寔曰獻神明皇帝。

translations.literal: and his father Shi the posthumous title Emperor Xianshenming.
translations.idiomatic: and his father Shi Emperor Xianshenming.

sentences.zh: 魏之舊俗，孟夏祀天及東廟，季夏帥眾卻霜於陰山，孟秋祀天於西郊。

translations.literal: By Wei's old custom, in the first month of summer they sacrificed to Heaven and the Eastern Temple; in the last month of summer they led the multitude to ward off frost at Mount Yin; in the first month of autumn they sacrificed to Heaven at the western suburb.
translations.idiomatic: By old Wei custom, in early summer they sacrificed to Heaven and the eastern temple; in late summer they led the people to ward off frost at Mount Yin; in early autumn they sacrificed to Heaven at the western suburb.

sentences.zh: 至是，始依仿古制，定郊廟朝饗禮樂，然惟孟夏祀天親行，其餘多有司攝事。

translations.literal: At this time they first followed ancient models, fixed the ritual and music for suburban, temple, court, and feast sacrifices — yet only the early-summer sacrifice to Heaven did the emperor perform in person; for the rest, officials mostly acted in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Now, for the first time, they modeled themselves on antiquity and fixed the ritual and music for suburban, temple, court, and feast sacrifices. Only the early-summer sacrifice to Heaven did the emperor perform in person; officials handled the rest.

sentences.zh: 又用崔宏議，自謂黃帝之後，以土德王。

translations.literal: Following Cui Hong's proposal, he declared himself a descendant of the Yellow Emperor and took Earth as his ruling virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On Cui Hong's advice he declared himself a descendant of the Yellow Emperor and adopted the virtue of Earth as his dynastic element.

sentences.zh: 徙六州二十二郡守宰、豪傑二千家於代都，東至代郡，西及善無，南極陰館，北盡參合，皆為畿內，其外四方、四維置八部師以監之。

translations.literal: He moved the administrators and leading families of twenty-two commanderies in six provinces — two thousand households — to the capital at Dai; east to Dai Commandery, west to Shanyang, south to the limit of Yinguan, north to Canhe — all became the inner domain; beyond this, in the four directions and four corners, eight division commanders were established to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated two thousand leading families and their officials from twenty-two commanderies in six provinces to the capital at Dai. From Dai Commandery in the east to Shanyang in the west, Yinguan in the south, and Canhe in the north, all became the inner domain. Beyond that he placed eight division commanders in the four directions and four corners to keep watch.

sentences.zh: 己亥，燕幽州刺史慕容豪、尚書左僕射張通、昌黎尹張順坐謀反誅。

translations.literal: On day jihai Murong Hao, Inspector of You Province of Yan; Zhang Tong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; and Zhang Shun, Magistrate of Changli, were executed on charges of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day Murong Hao, inspector of You, Zhang Tong, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and Zhang Shun, magistrate of Changli, were executed for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 初，琅邪人孫泰學妖術於錢唐杜子恭，士民多奉之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sun Tai of Langye studied sorcery under Du Zigong of Qiantang, and many gentry and commoners revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tai of Langye had studied occult arts under Du Zigong of Qiantang, and many townspeople followed him.

sentences.zh: 王珣惡之，流泰於廣州。

translations.literal: Wang Xun hated this and banished Tai to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun despised him and exiled Sun Tai to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王雅薦泰於孝武帝，雲知養性之方，召還，累官至新安太守。

translations.literal: Wang Ya recommended Tai to Emperor Xiaowu, saying he knew methods for nurturing life; Tai was recalled and rose through successive posts to Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya recommended him to Emperor Xiaowu as a master of the arts of longevity. Sun Tai was recalled and eventually rose to prefect of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 泰知晉祚將終，因王恭之亂，以討恭為名，收合兵眾，聚貨巨億，三吳之人多從之。

translations.literal: Tai knew the Jin dynasty's mandate was nearing its end; taking advantage of Wang Gong's rebellion, he gathered troops under the pretext of punishing Gong, amassed wealth in the hundreds of millions, and many people of the Three Wu regions followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tai saw that the Jin mandate was failing. Using Wang Gong's rebellion as his pretext, he raised troops to "punish Gong," amassed a fortune in the hundreds of millions, and won many followers across the Three Wu region.

sentences.zh: 識者皆憂其為亂，以中領軍元顯與之善，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Those who understood the situation all feared he would bring turmoil, but because Central Army Commander Yuan Xian was on good terms with him, no one dared speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment feared he would rebel, but because Yuan Xian, the central army commander, was his friend, no one dared report him.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史謝輶發其謀，己酉，會稽王道子使元顯誘而斬之，並其六子。

translations.literal: Xie You, Internal Administrator of Kuaiji, exposed his plot; on day jiyou Simao Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, had Yuan Xian lure and execute him, together with his six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Xie You, internal administrator of Kuaiji, exposed the plot. On jiyou day Simao Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, had Yuan Xian lure Sun Tai out and execute him along with his six sons.

sentences.zh: 兄子恩逃入海，愚民猶以為泰蟬蛻不死，就海中資給恩。

translations.literal: His nephew En fled into the sea; foolish people still believed Tai had cast off his shell like a cicada and was not dead, and went to the sea to supply En.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew En fled to the sea. Simple folk still believed Sun Tai had shed his body like a cicada and lived on, and they took supplies to En by sea.

sentences.zh: 恩乃聚合亡命，得百餘人，以謀復仇。

translations.literal: En then gathered fugitives and obtained more than a hundred men to plot revenge.
translations.idiomatic: En gathered more than a hundred outlaws and began plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 西平王禿髮烏孤更稱武威王。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu, King of Xiping, again styled himself King of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu, King of Xiping, took the title King of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 是歲，楊盛遣使附魏，魏以盛為仇池王。」」

translations.literal: That year Yang Sheng sent envoys to attach himself to Wei, and Wei made Sheng King of Chouji.””
translations.idiomatic: That year Yang Sheng sent envoys to submit to Wei, and Wei made him King of Chouji.””
